cells.remarks: Fragment of stone lying near the Baṭṭērappa temple now preserved in the museum of Kannada Research Office, Dharwar. This fragment of stone bears an inscription in archaic Kannada characters of the 7th century A. D. It refers to Bādāmi as Vijaya-Vaṭapya- [dhistha]na "the victorious metropolis of Vātāpi " and gives the preamble beginning with Parama - Bhagavataṇam Svami - Mahasena - Matrigana - Padanuahyatanam etc. Polekēsi - vallabha i. e. Pulikēsin I is mentioned as the performer of a horse sacrifice. From the alphabet and the mention of Vātāpi as the victorious capital, it appears probable that the inscription belongs to the reign of Pulikēsin II who established himself at Vātāpi after a successful campaign of digvijaya as recorded in the famous Aihole inscription of A. D. 634. It is interesting to note that the record begins with the mention of the capital city in the words Svasti śrīmad - vijaya - Vātā- pyadhishṭhānē, with the prefix vijaya, on the analogy of vijaya- Vaijayantyām (in the victorious city of Vaijayanti i.e. Banavāsi) of the early Kadamba inscriptions of the 5th and 6th centuries A. D. See Nos. 2 and 3 below where a similar prefix Vijaya and affix adhisthāna are given to Vātāpi.

cells.remarks: Pillar in the Jambulinga temple. This inscription belongs to the reign of Vijayāditya - Satyāśraya and bears the date Jyeshtha Paurṇima of Saka 621 falling in the third regnal year of the king. It is engraved in very cursive characters of the period which are not quite distinct in some places. The grant portion in lines 10-15 is written in archaic Kannada language, which is referred to as Prākṛita - bhāṣha in line 9 f. Lines 1-10 are written in Sanskrit. The inscription records the installation of the gods Brahmā, Vishṇu and Mahēśvara at the capital city of Vatapyadhisthāna which is adorned by several thousands of excellent dvijas endowed with the knowledge of fourteen sciences (vidyā) and was highly esteemed by the great kings headed by Satyāśraya ", by the king's mother (1) The continuation is lost. 2 No. 2. -- Bādāmi inscription of Vijayāditya-Satyāśraya, Saka 621. R. S. Panchamukhi. Scale: one-fifth. ( rāja-mātṛā ) Vinayavati. It further registers a gift of several taxes ( śulka ) and incomes in kind, evidently made by her for the benefit of the temple of the triad. These are specified in ll. 11-15. The inscription is published in Ind. Ant. Vol. X, p. 60 by Dr. Fleet. But only the first 10 lines have been deciphered. Here the expression Vinayavatīyā rājamā[tṛā] has been wrongly read as Vijayavatyām rājadhānyām. The second letter is clearly ma and not ja and dhānyām is only māt[ṛā]. The place where the installation of images was made is given already in line 3 as 'Vātāpyadhishṭhāne' and the mention of it again as 'vijayavatyām rājadhānyām' would be super- fluous and misleading. The name of the king's mother Vinayavati is disclosed here for the first time. Since the third regnal year fell in Śaka 621, Jyeṣṭha, Paurnamāsī ( A. D. 699, May 20 ) and the Vishuva day in the bright half of Āśvajuja occurred in the third month of the thirteenth regnal year, according to the Aihole inscription published in Ind. Ant. Vol. XIII, p. 284, the first year of Vijayāditya's reign must have commenced in Śaka 618, Āshādha i. e. in July, A. D. 696. [Kannada original] [English translation, Gemini-rendered, verify] Vāsudēva-guru (disciple) Prabhāchandra The inscription may be assigned to the period anterior to or contemporaneous with that of Kirtivarmarasa to whom the second record that follows it, belongs. The second record refers itself to the reign Prithvi-vallabha Rajadhi- raja Paramesvara Kirtivarmarasa and introduces Sindarasa as administering Gangi-Pāṇdivūru. Parameśvara Madhavatti-arasa is stated to have been requested by the Gamundas and Karanas who, with his permission, granted, by rājamāna (royal measuring rod), eight mattar of wet land ( galde ) below (a tank) to the west of Kammagalūru for worship and offerings in the temple of Jinēndra. Prabhāchandra-Gurava belonging to (bali) the chēdiya of Paralūru was the recipient of the gift. This person is evidently identical with the disciple of Vāsudēva - guru mentioned in the previous grant. The record is important as it furnishes a specimen of archaic Kannada, current in the 8th century A. D. The verbs ittr, salippor and kidippor (1. 20) are noteworthy. The expressions [ava]rtē dharma (1. 19 f) and avartē pāpa (1. 20) exhibit a close affinity with the Tamil idioms avardai-darnam and avardai pāpam. Guru or Gurāva suffixed to the names of Vāsudēva and Prabhāchandra are variant forms of Gorava of later inscriptions (cf. Mōni-gorava of No. 14 below, line 8). The king Kirtivarmarasa has to be identified with Kirtivarman II on account of the epithet Rājādirāja Parameśvara borne by him. For, it is stated in the Aihole inscription of Pulikēśin II dated A. D. 634, that Pulikēśin II was the first to assume the biruda Rājādhirājā Parameśvara after vanquishing the great North-Indian monarch Harshavardhana. The name, Sindarasa indicates the existence of Sinda rule in this early period. cells.remarks: Stone brought from Adūr now preserved in the museum of Kannada Research Office, Dharwar. About 750 A. D. The subjoined inscription contains two records - one in lines 1-14 and the other in lines 15-20. They are both engraved in the same archaic Kannada alphabet which was current in the Deccan in the 7th and 8th centuries A. D. The first record is couched in Sanskrit and the second in a specimen of ancient Kannada. The first record opens with an invocation to Vardhamāna the twenty- fourth Tirthankara and seems to introduce a certain chief who on a request (vijñāpanēna) is stated to have granted land measuring twenty-five vivartanas for the promotion of the Jinalaya and of alms-house con- structed by a Gamunda whose name is probably Dharma-Gāmuṇḍa given in l. 14 below. The grant was publicly announced and attested by Uchchorinda and others.1 Then follow three imprecatory verses beginning with Svadattam pradattam, Svan - datum su-mahach- chhakyam and Bahubhir vasudha bhukta. Since the writing is effaced in many places, full details about the donor and the donation are not legible. The stone tablet is stated to have been set up by Śrīpala grand- son of Dharma - Gamunda a disciple of Prabha [chandra] whose lineage is specified as follows :- Vinayanandi of the Paralūra-gama (disciple) [Footnote 1] The expression Uñchchōrinda - pradhānakān may also be interpreted as "chief officers of Uñchchōrinda". whom Kadamba Krishnavarman I is stated, in the Dēvagiri copper-plates of yuvarāja Dēvavarman, to have subdued (Sāmanta-rāja-viśeṣaratna- Nāgajān = ākramya) (Ind. Ant. Vol. VII. p. 33), were represented by the family of the Sinda chiefs to which Sindarasa belonged, in the 5th century A. D. in this part of the original Kadamba territory where the present inscription is found. Another name which is noteworthy in the second inscription is Madhavatti-arasa which in all probability is an abbreviation of Mādhava- satti-arasa. If this is correct, it would apparently be a Sēndraka name which usually ends in satti or śakti. The Sēndrakas who like the Sindas traced their descent to the Nāgas were subordinate to the Chalukyas from the beginning of the latter's career. The following chiefs of the family are known so far:- Name of the Sēndraka chief. King. Bhānusakti (Ind. Ant. Vol. VI, p. 31) : Kadamba Harivarman Vānasatti-arasa (No. 32 of Bombay-Karnatak Collection for 1933-34). Durgaśakti, son of Kundaśakti and grand- son of Vijayāśakti (Ind. Ant. Vol. VII, p. : Pulikēsin II 106). Bhima-śakti (Nos. 125 and 127 of Bombay- Karnatak Collection for 1928-29). Sēnānanda (Ep. Ind. Vol. III, p. 51). Dēvaśakti (J. B. B. R. A. Vol. XVI, pp. 227, } 238) : Vikramāditya I Sēndraka-Mahārāja Pogilli (J. B. B. R. A. S. Vol. XIX, p. 142). : Vinayāditya. Jayasakti, son of Nikumbhalla-śakti, grand- son of Adityaśakti and great-grandson of Bhānusakti (Bharata Itihāsa Saṃśōdhaka : Vikramāditya II. Maṇḍala Quarterly, Śaka, 1834, p. 169). Adhirāja Indrananda son of Vijayananda- } Favourite of Madhynamarāja (Ep. Ind. Vol. XIX, p. 289) : Rāshtrakūṭa Dejja-Mahārāja. Sēndraka Nāgaśakti (Mys. Arch. Rep. 1909) : Kirtivarman II. 6 No. 3. Ādūr inscription of Kirttivarmarasa (Kirttivarman II) Madhava[sa*]tti would be a new name in this family. The epithet Paramēśvara applied to him is inexplicable. (1) I Inscription. d dhana vya[(kri)]s(t)yana s(ā)tā[ka]vu . [svō] . . . . . . rṛ(kṣ)akīya(n) s(t)ra(kṣ)a . sahasyān(n)i niṃbhyaryyāṇō [j(j)ānō] - (1) Paramēśvara i.e. Kīrtivarmarasa (l. 15) requested Mādhavatti-arasa. But it is impossible that the king should have requested a subor- dinate chief. (2) Mādhavatti bore the epithet Paramēśvara which is an imperial title. This is unlikely. (3) The Gāmuṇḍas and Karanas made a request to Paramēśvara i.e. king as well as to Mādhavatti-arasa who must have held an important position in the administration. In this case the text paramēśvaraṃ mādhavattiyarasanāgarkkage nijaṃ jānaṃ gēlsuyg etc. just as kōtuyām kōlārgai māṃ śri(śrē)ṣṭhige kotti(ṭṭ)anḍ(n) means kōtuyāmakke kōlārgam śrēṣṭhige kottiṭṭanḍu. text.remarks:
Stone brought from Adūr now preserved in the museum of Kannada
Research Office, Dharwar.
About 750 A. D.
The subjoined inscription contains two records - one in lines 1-14
and the other in lines 15-20. They are both engraved in the same
archaic Kannada alphabet which was current in the Deccan in the 7th
and 8th centuries A. D. The first record is couched in Sanskrit and the
second in a specimen of ancient Kannada.
The first record opens with an invocation to Vardhamāna the twenty-
fourth Tirthankara and seems to introduce a certain chief who on a
request (vijñāpanēna) is stated to have granted land measuring twenty-five
vivartanas for the promotion of the Jinalaya and of alms-house con-
structed by a Gamunda whose name is probably Dharma-Gāmuṇḍa
given in l. 14 below. The grant was publicly announced and attested
by Uchchorinda and others.1 Then follow three imprecatory
verses beginning with Svadattam pradattam, Svan - datum su-mahach-
chhakyam and Bahubhir vasudha bhukta. Since the writing is effaced in
many places, full details about the donor and the donation are not
legible. The stone tablet is stated to have been set up by Śrīpala grand-
son of Dharma - Gamunda a disciple of Prabha [chandra] whose lineage is
specified as follows :-
Vinayanandi of the Paralūra-gama
(disciple)
[Footnote 1] The expression Uñchchōrinda - pradhānakān may also be interpreted as
"chief officers of Uñchchōrinda".
whom Kadamba Krishnavarman I is stated, in the Dēvagiri copper-plates
of yuvarāja Dēvavarman, to have subdued (Sāmanta-rāja-viśeṣaratna-
Nāgajān = ākramya) (Ind. Ant. Vol. VII. p. 33), were represented
by the family of the Sinda chiefs to which Sindarasa belonged, in the
5th century A. D. in this part of the original Kadamba territory where
the present inscription is found.
Another name which is noteworthy in the second inscription is
Madhavatti-arasa which in all probability is an abbreviation of Mādhava-
satti-arasa. If this is correct, it would apparently be a Sēndraka name
which usually ends in satti or śakti. The Sēndrakas who like the Sindas
traced their descent to the Nāgas were subordinate to the Chalukyas
from the beginning of the latter's career. The following chiefs of
the family are known so far:-

cells.remarks: On a rock near the Stbāraḍoṇi on the way to Mahākūṭa. The inscription is in two lines of one verse in Sanskrit and is engraved in archaic Kannada alphabet of the 8th century A. D. It states that death is preferable to dishonour, for the former gives instantaneous pain while the latter gives mortification, day after day. The sentiment expressed here may be compared with the oft-quoted foot Sambhavitasyacha-kirtir-maranad-atirichyatē of the Bhagavadgītā, (chpt. II, v. 34). It is not possible, to know who and under what circumstances, had this couplet incised on the rock. In another place at Bādāmi this verse is engraved on the rock while describing the greatness of Kappe-arabhaṭṭan who appears to have been put to an unbearable victimisation and consequently killed himself in preference to enduring the unspecified dishonour done to him (Ind. Ant. Vol. X, p. 61).

cells.remarks: Stone standing inside the compound wall of the Mamletdar's Office. This undated inscription belongs to the reign of Amōghavarsha I and introduces his subordinate Baṅkeyarasa of the Chellakētana family as administering Banavāsi - 12,000, Belgali - 300, Kundarage - 70, Kundūr - 500 and Purigere - 300 districts, and Baṅkeya's son Kundaṭṭe as ruling over Niḍugundage - 12. It is stated that Kundaṭṭe and Rāpa made a grant of one mattar of garden-land and five mattar of cultivable land (keyyu) for the temple of Mahādēva belonging to Kuppaṇṇa, the perggaḍe of Niḍugundage - 12, for the merit of Baṅkeya (Baṅkeyaṅge dharmmam = akk-endu). The sentence in lines 13-16 has an involved construction and its sense is as follows:- "ಮಣ್ಣಂ ತನ್ನ ಭಾಗಮಂ ಕುಡೆ, ಆ ವಜ್ಜಾರ ಕುಪ್ಪಂ ದೆಗುಲಮಂ ಮಾಡಿ ಸಣ್ಣಾಥ ಪರಿಹಾರಂ ಪದೆದೊಂ." Here vaṭṭāra means an enclosure or site. In the paranthetical clause in ll. 15-16, Śaṅkara is stated to be the Nālgāmuṇḍa and Gāḍiyamma the trustee of the gift-land. Fleet who published this inscription in Ep. Ind. Vol. VII, pp. 212-13 interpreted vaṭṭāra as a corruption of bhaṭṭāra 'venerable' which is unlikely, and thought that Gāḍiyamma mentioned in the paranthetical clause was the donee. Further his interpretation of ondu-ttaram (l. 3) as meaning (sixty) plus one, lacks the support of epigraphical evidence since the expression is found used in the sense of uttarōttaram 'progressively' in the Annigeri inscription of Kīrtivarman II (Ep. Ind. Vol. XXI, 207), Venkaṭapur inscription (No. 82 of Bombay [Footnote 1] Fleet's interpretation of line 10 that Kundaṭṭe said to Baṅkeya - "Let there be a religious grant" is apparently not correct. [Footnote 2] The sentence may be translated as follows:- "On Maḷḍa giving his own share, Kuppa caused the temple to be made in that site (vaṭṭāra), and obtained the property free from all imposts while Śaṅkara was the Nālgāmuṇḍa and Gāḍiyamma was the trustee (made) it permanent (nile). If vaṭṭāra can be a variant of vaḍḍāra, (vaḍḍāra) it will be an adjective to Kuppa meaning "Kuppa of the stone-cutters"." 16 Karnatak Collection for 1926-27 ) and an inscription from Mysore (Ep. Carn. Vol. VII, Sorab 88 ) the last two belonging to Krishna II. This and the previous inscription are important for a study of the evolution of Kannada alphabet during the early Rāshtrakūṭa period. 17 [Kannada original] [English translation, Gemini-rendered, verify]

text.remarks:
Stone standing inside the compound wall of the Mamletdar's Office.
This undated inscription belongs to the reign of Amōghavarsha I and introduces his subordinate Baṅkeyarasa of the Chellakētana family as administering Banavāsi - 12,000, Belgali - 300, Kundarage - 70, Kundūr - 500 and Purigere - 300 districts, and Baṅkeya's son Kundaṭṭe as ruling over Niḍugundage - 12. It is stated that Kundaṭṭe and Rāpa made a grant of one mattar of garden-land and five mattar of cultivable land (keyyu) for the temple of Mahādēva belonging to Kuppaṇṇa, the perggaḍe of Niḍugundage - 12, for the merit of Baṅkeya (Baṅkeyaṅge dharmmam = akk-endu). The sentence in lines 13-16 has an involved construction and its sense is as follows:- "ಮಣ್ಣಂ ತನ್ನ ಭಾಗಮಂ ಕುಡೆ, ಆ ವಜ್ಜಾರ ಕುಪ್ಪಂ ದೆಗುಲಮಂ ಮಾಡಿ ಸಣ್ಣಾಥ ಪರಿಹಾರಂ ಪದೆದೊಂ." Here vaṭṭāra means an enclosure or site. In the paranthetical clause in ll. 15-16, Śaṅkara is stated to be the Nālgāmuṇḍa and Gāḍiyamma the trustee of the gift-land.
Fleet who published this inscription in Ep. Ind. Vol. VII, pp. 212-13 interpreted vaṭṭāra as a corruption of bhaṭṭāra 'venerable' which is unlikely, and thought that Gāḍiyamma mentioned in the paranthetical clause was the donee. Further his interpretation of ondu-ttaram (l. 3) as meaning (sixty) plus one, lacks the support of epigraphical evidence since the expression is found used in the sense of uttarōttaram 'progressively' in the Annigeri inscription of Kīrtivarman II (Ep. Ind. Vol. XXI, 207), Venkaṭapur inscription (No. 82 of Bombay
[Footnote 1] Fleet's interpretation of line 10 that Kundaṭṭe said to Baṅkeya - "Let there be a religious grant" is apparently not correct.
[Footnote 2] The sentence may be translated as follows:-
"On Maḷḍa giving his own share, Kuppa caused the temple to be made in that site (vaṭṭāra), and obtained the property free from all imposts while Śaṅkara was the Nālgāmuṇḍa and Gāḍiyamma was the trustee (made) it permanent (nile). If vaṭṭāra can be a variant of vaḍḍāra, (vaḍḍāra) it will be an adjective to Kuppa meaning "Kuppa of the stone-cutters"."

This and the previous inscription are important for a study of the evolution of Kannada alphabet during the early Rāshtrakūṭa period.

cells.remarks: Inscribed stone standing inside near the compound wall (on the back side) of Mamletdar's Office. This badly damaged and mutilated inscription refers itself to the reign of Nityavarsha Prithivivallabha (Indra III) and introduces his subordinate Mahāsāmanta Baṅkeyarasa as the governor of a Thirty-two Thousand province whose name is lost. Then a certain [Suriga] Chāmuṇḍa is enlogised in ll. 5-7. On the date specified in lines 7-10, Chāmuṇḍa is stated to have discerned life as devoid of essence and happiness and appears to have made a gift. Since the stone is broken away at this point the details of the gift are not clear. The details of date are given as follows: Śaka 841 (in words) Pramathin, Magha, su. padiva. Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti. The Uttarāya- ṇa-Saṅkrānti had occurred 3 days earlier i. e. on Thursday, December 23, A. D. 919; other details regularly corresponded to Sunday, December, 26, A. D. 919. It may be recalled that an inscription at Daṇḍāpura issued on the day of Makara (Uttarāyana)-Saṅkrānti in Śaka 840 (expired), Pramāthin, refers itself to the reign of Prabhūtavarsha Govinda IV. It has been held by Fleet that Nityavarsha (Indra III) was succeeded by Govinda IV, some time before Śaka 840 (Ep. Ind. Vol. VI, pp. 176-77). Recent discoveries mentioning Nityavarsha as king in records dated subsequent to Śaka 840 i. e. in Śaka 848, 850 etc. have led some scholars to think that Nityavarsha of these records was Govinda IV who like his father (Indra III) is supposed to have borné the biruda Nityavarsha (A. R. No. 277 of 1918, 235 of 1937-38, and A. S. R. 1929-30, p. 173, ibid, 1930-34 pt. I, pp. 235 and 244). But Nitya- varsha was the distinguishing epithet of Indra III, who is always referred to by that biruda in the stone and copper-plate inscriptions of his and subsequent periods. (See the Hattimattūr inscription, Asūti inscription, Cambay plates, Saṅgli charter, Kalas inscription etc.) For a detailed examination of the problem, see Introduction to this volume. * ||| [Footnote 1] Broken after this. 18 19

cells.remarks: Inscription stone standing inside the compound wall of the Mamletdar's Office. This is a mutilated and damaged record belonging to the reign of Trailokyamalladeva (Somesvara I). It introduces his son Vikramaditya- deva with all the Ganga epithets such as the lord of Kuvalalapura, Nanda- girinatha, Nanniya-Ganga, Ganga-Permanadi etc., as governing the Gangavadi-96,000 and Banavasi-12,000 provinces. His subordinate chief was Mahamandalesvara Harikesarideva of the Kadamba family who is described with a long list of birudas in ll. 10-15. He was governing Banavasi-12,000 with his queen Lachchaladevi who is extolled in the few verses in ll. 19-27. The chief Harikesarideva and queen Lachchaladevi in conjunction with (the members of) the Panchamatha- sthana and the general body (Mahajana) of the trade guilds (Nagara- mahajana) and the padinaruvaru (the sixteen representatives?) granted the request of Dusiga Ketisetti, the village Pallavura as talavritti, the access derived from the taxes siddhaya (income-tax), kirudere, kirukula, dayadramma, house-tax and military tax (dandaya) etc., for the benefit of the temple of Kadambesvaradeva, into the hands of Somesvara-Panditadeva. The village which was included in Nidugundage - 12 a circle or subdivision in Panungal-500 district is stated to have been turned into a Naishthika-sthana ('a seat for Naishthika asceties') before it was endowed. his son, or his wife or near the Vaishnava (fire) in the absence of the former. He is described as follows in the Garudapurana : नैष्ठिको ब्रह्मचारी च वसेदाचार्यसन्निधौ । तदभावेऽस्य तनये पत्न्यां वस्त्रांतरे वा ॥ अनेन विधिना देहं साधयेद्विजितेन्द्रियः ॥ Lines 36-38 record a gift of taxes made for the same temple by Mahamandalesvara Satyasrayadeva described as Banavasi-puravare- svara. Some minor gifts of land are also registered in ll. 44-49, for the renovation and repairs of the temple, for Vidyadana (imparting of education) and for various services in the temple. The inscription was composed by Perggade Ketisetti and engraved by Kaloja. The details of date are :- Saka 977, Manmathe, Paushya, su. 13, Monday, Uttarayana-Sankranti, Vyatipata. They are irregular. In the given year, the Uttarayana-Sankranti occurred on Sunday, Paushya, su. not Monday as cited in the record. If su. 13 is a mistake for su. 3, the English equivalent of the date would be probably Monday, December 25, observed after the moment of its occurrence. text.remarks:
Inscription stone standing inside the compound wall of the Mamletdar's Office.
This is a mutilated and damaged record belonging to the reign of
Trailokyamalladeva (Somesvara I). It introduces his son Vikramaditya-
deva with all the Ganga epithets such as the lord of Kuvalalapura, Nanda-
girinatha, Nanniya-Ganga, Ganga-Permanadi etc., as governing the
Gangavadi-96,000 and Banavasi-12,000 provinces. His subordinate
chief was Mahamandalesvara Harikesarideva of the Kadamba family
who is described with a long list of birudas in ll. 10-15. He was
governing Banavasi-12,000 with his queen Lachchaladevi who is extolled
in the few verses in ll. 19-27. The chief Harikesarideva and queen
Lachchaladevi in conjunction with (the members of) the Panchamatha-
sthana and the general body (Mahajana) of the trade guilds (Nagara-
mahajana) and the padinaruvaru (the sixteen representatives?) granted
the request of Dusiga Ketisetti, the village Pallavura as talavritti,
the access derived from the taxes siddhaya (income-tax),
kirudere, kirukula, dayadramma, house-tax and military tax (dandaya)
etc., for the benefit of the temple of Kadambesvaradeva, into the hands
of Somesvara-Panditadeva. The village which was included in
Nidugundage - 12 a circle or subdivision in Panungal-500 district is stated
to have been turned into a Naishthika-sthana ('a seat for Naishthika
asceties') before it was endowed.
his son, or his wife or near the Vaishnava (fire) in the absence of the former.
He is described as follows in the Garudapurana :
नैष्ठिको ब्रह्मचारी च वसेदाचार्यसन्निधौ ।
तदभावेऽस्य तनये पत्न्यां वस्त्रांतरे वा ॥
अनेन विधिना देहं साधयेद्विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
Lines 36-38 record a gift of taxes made for the same temple by
Mahamandalesvara Satyasrayadeva described as Banavasi-puravare-
svara. Some minor gifts of land are also registered in ll. 44-49, for
the renovation and repairs of the temple, for Vidyadana (imparting of
education) and for various services in the temple.
The inscription was composed by Perggade Ketisetti and engraved
by Kaloja.
The details of date are :- Saka 977, Manmathe, Paushya, su. 13,
Monday, Uttarayana-Sankranti, Vyatipata. They are irregular. In the
given year, the Uttarayana-Sankranti occurred on Sunday, Paushya, su.
not Monday as cited in the record. If su. 13 is a mistake for su. 3, the
English equivalent of the date would be probably Monday, December 25,
observed after the moment of its occurrence.

ಧ್ಯಾನಧಾರಣಮೋನಾನುಷ್ಠಾನ ಜ-32 ಪನಮಾದಿ ಸಂಪನ್ನ ರಪ್ಪ ಶ್ರೀ ಮತ್ಕೇಮ್ಯೋಮೇಶ್ವರ ಪಣ್ಣಿತ ದೇವಗೆ ಶ್ರೀ ಮದರಿ-33 ಕಸನ ದೇವನುಂ ಪ್ರಧಾನಮನಿಟ್ಟು ಸ್ವೀಕೃತ ಸನ್ನಮಂ ಪೂಜಾಭಕ್ತಿಯೊಳು ನಡೆಸಹಾನುಂಗೆಯ್ಯು ಅಣಕಕಣ್ಣುಂ ನಿಡಗುಂ.34 ನೈಗೆ ಪನ್ನೇರಡಜ ಬಲಿಯ ಪಳ್ಳಪುರಂತಳ್ಯತೀಯಾಗೆ ದೇವಗೆ ಸಿದ್ಧಾಯಂ ಕಿರುದೇವ ಕಿಲುಕುಳನವಾಯ ಪ್ರಸ್ನಮ-35 ನೇನಂ ದಕ್ಷಾಯಂ ಸರ್ವಾಭ್ಯಂತರ ಸಿದ್ಧಿಂ ಸವ್ಯನಮಸ್ಯವ್ಯಾಗಿ ಬಟ್ಟಿರಿದಂ ಪಳ್ಳಮಹಾನಮ ನಮಂ ಪಡಿದುವರುಂ36 ನಕರಮುಮಿಸ್ಸ ಧಮ್ಮಮಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾಲಿಸುವುದು (1) ಸಮಧಿಕ ಪಞ್ಚ ಮಹಾಸಬ್ದಮಹಾಸಾಮಂತೇಶ್ವರ37 ನವಾಚೀ ಪುರವಧೀಶ್ವರಂ ಬಂಟರ ಬವಂ ಕಚ್ಚುಯಂ ದೋಣಂ ಗಣ್ಣರ ಚೂಜು ಶ್ರೀಮತ್ಕೃತಾಕ್ಷಯ ದೇವಗೆರ್ನಾಲತ್ತೆ-38 ಯೊಲ್ಲಯಂ ಚನ್ನಾಕ್ಯಸಗಾಯ ಸವ್ಯನಮಸ್ಯವ್ಯಾಗಿ (2) ದೇವಪುರದ ನಿವೇದ್ಯದ ಕಲ್ಯು ಪ್ರದೋಟಿಟದ ಕಿಮ39 ಶಿಮೆ (3) ದೇವನ ತಳ್ಯತೀಯಾರ ಪೂಲದ ಶಿಮೆ ಮೂದಲದ್ದೆ ವೆಟ್ಟ | ಅಗ್ನೇಯಕ್ಕೆ ಕಲ್ಲಪುಂಜಿಗೆ | ತೆಂಕಲು ಲಿಂಗದ ಕಲ್ಲು |42 ನೈಋತ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಕಲ್ಲಗುಟ್ಟಿ | ಪಡುವಣಲಗಟ್ಟದ ಕಜಿಯೊಳೆ ಶಿಮೆ || ವಾಯುವ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಬಸರಿಯಕೊಳ | ಬಡಗಲು ಕಲ್ಲು |43 ಕಜಿಯೊಳಗೆಣ ಲೆ ಬಾವಿ | ಈಶಾನ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ತಿರುವಟ್ಟಿ | ಇಲ್ಮೀ ಚತುರಾಶ್ರಯಶಿಮೆ (4)44 ಭೋಗ ಕಣ್ಮ ಸ್ಯಟಿಕ ಜೀಣ್ಯ ದ್ಯಾರಕ್ಕೆ[ಂ] ರಾಜಮಾನ ದಂಡಲು ಮತ್ತರನ್ನಯ |ಜತ್ತಕ್ಕೆ | ಮತ್ತಂ45 ರ್ ಪನ್ನೇರಡು ವಿದ್ಯಾಧಾನಕ್ಕೆ ಮತ್ತಲು ಪನ್ನೇರಡು | ಗಾವಣ್ಣರುಣ್ಣಲ ಮತ್ತರಪನ್ನೇರಡು ಅಡವಕ್ಕಂ46 ಗ ಕೀತಿಕ್ಕಿಟ್ಟಗ ತೇಜಂ ಗಣತಿಗೆ ಮತ್ತರ್ ಪನ್ನೇರಡು | ಪಜಿಕಾರಗೆ ಮತ್ತರಪತ್ತು ಗಾವಣ್ಣರ್ಗೆ47 ಪೆಗ್ಗಡಗೆ ಮತ್ತಲಾಲ | ಪಿರಿಯದೊಗೆ ಮತ್ತರಾಲ | ಕಳವ ನಾಲ್ಗೆ ಮತ್ತರಿಚ್ಚಾತ್ಯ ಎರ್ದ48 ತ್ತು | ಓಲಗದ ಸುಳಿಯರುಜುವಗ್ಗ ಮತ್ತರನ್ನಲ್ | ಸೂಳ | ವಳಂಗಿ ಮತ್ತರಯ್ಯು |49 ದೇವನ ಕೈಯೊಳಗೆ ಕಲ್ಲಿಸದೊಜಂಗ ಮತ್ತರಯ್ಯು (5) ಇನ್ನೀ ಧಮ್ಮಮಂ ಅರಿಂಪ್ಯಾರ ಪೂಜಾಫಲ50 ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಯ ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಂ ಕೌದಾರಂ ಶ್ರೀಶೈಲಂ ಗಂಗೆ ಗಂಗಾಸಾಗರಂ-ಗಳೆಬಾದಿಯ ತೀರ್ಥಂ51 ಪಞ್ಚರತ್ನಂಗಳು ಕೊಡೆಲು ಕೊಳ್ಳಗುಮಂ ಕಲ್ಲಿಸಿ ಸಾಸಿವ್ವರ ಚತುರ್ವೇದ ಪಾರಗರಪ್ಪ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಗೆ ಉಭ52 ಕ್ಕ | ಎಳ್ಳೋಟಿ ತಪೋಧನಗೆ ವಾರಣಾಸಿಯೊಳ್ ಮಹಾ ಭೋಜನಂ ಮಾಡಿ [ನ*]ದ*] ಫಳಮಂ | [ಇ*]ಂತೀ ಧಮ್ಮಮಂ53 ಬಟ್ಟಿರಿದನುಂ ಪೆಲ್ಲವ ತೂ ತೀರ್ಥಂಗಳೊಳ್ ಸಾಸಿರ ಕಪಿಲೆಯುಂ ಸಾಸಿರ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರುವೆಳ್ಳೋಟಿ ತಪೋ54 ಪಾಶಕನಕ್ಕ (6) ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯಂಯಂ ಧಮ್ಮಸೇತು ಶ್ರೀಪಾಣಂ ಕಾಳೇ ಕಾಳೇ ಪಾಲನೀಯೋ ಭವದ್ಭಿಃ | ಸನ್ಮಾನೇ55 ಯೋ ಭವೀಯೋ ಯಾಚತೇ ರಾಮಭದ್ರಃ || ಬಹುಭ್ಯಸ್ಸುಧಾ ಭುಕ್ತಾ ರಾಜಭಿಃಸಗರಾದಿಭಿಃ ಯಸ್ಯ56 ತಸ್ಯ ತದಾ ಫಲಂ | ಬೆಸಗೆಯ ಮಂಗಲ ಮಹಾಶ್ರೀ ಶ್ರೀ (9)

cells.language: Kannada and Sanskrit
cells.remarks: Inscription stone standing inside near the compound wall of the Mamletdar's Office. The record belongs to the reign of Tribhuvanamalladeva (Vikramaditya VI) and introduces his subordinate Mahamandalesvara Tailapadeva the lord of Banavasi-pura, an ornament of the Kadambas as governing Panungal-500 on the ubhaya-samya tenure and Maragavunda of Nidugundage as the Gavunda (revenue officer) of the village. On the date specified in ll. 10-12, it is stated that Uttavasetti of Tilivalli, Mallisetti of (belonging to) Kanchaya, Akisetti of Doni Chamisetti belonging to Kariya Ketisetti - all together, granted for the temple of Mulasthanadeva, one visa for every heru, one visa on a visit (darkana), Hannavaniga Singana and the five hundred and four (Mahajanas of the place?) gave . . . for every heru, for the decoration of the deity (gatra). Ramesvara-Pandita is stated to be the officer in charge of these gifts. The details of date are:- Chalukya Vikrama year 32, Sarvajit, Chaitra, su. Padiva, Sunday. Sarvajit fell in Saka 1029 which was Ch. Vik. year 31. In this year the given tithi occurred on a Monday, (not Sunday) whereas for the next year i.e. Saka 1030, Sarvadharin which corresponded to Ch. Vik. year 32, the details regularly corresponded to Sunday, March 15, A. D. 1108. The cyclic year is evidently an expired one. I piece II piece [Footnote 1] The stone is broken away after this.
cells.text_original:
1 (1) ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಭುವನಶ್ರಯ ಶ್ರೀ ಪೃಥ್ವೀವಲ್ಲಭ
2 ಮಹಾರಾಜಾಧಿರಾಜ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ ಪರಮ ಭಟ್ಟಾರ
3 ಸತ್ಯಾಶ್ರಯ ಕುಳತಿಳಕ ಚಾಳುಕ್ಯಾಭರಣಂ ಶ್ರೀ
4 ಮತ್ರಿಭುವನಮಲ್ಲದೇವರ ವಿಜಯ ರಾಜ್ಯಮುತ್ತರೋತ್ತ
5 ರಾಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿ ಪ್ರವರ್ದ್ಧಮಾನಂ ಆಚಂದ್ರಾರ್ಕ ತಾರಂಬರಂ ಸಲು
6 ತ್ತಮಿರೇ ಸತ್ಯಾದವಿದ್ಯೋಪಜೀವನ ಸಮುಧಿಗತ ಪಂಚಮಹಾಸಬ್ದ ಮಹಾ
7 ಮಂಡಳೇಶ್ವರಂ ಬನವಾಸಿ ಪುರವರಾಧೀಶ್ವರಂ ಕದಂಬರಾ[ಭ]ರಣಂ [ಸಾ]-
8 ಮದಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ ಸಹಿತಂ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಮಹಾಮಂಡಳೇಶ್ವರಂ ಕೈಲ[ಪ]-
9 ದೇವರ್ ಪಾನಂಗಲ್ಲನ್ನುಮನುಭವಿಸುತ್ತಮಿರ್ದುದರಿಂ ಮಲೆ-
10 ಗುಂದೆಯ ಮಹಾಗಾವುಂಡ ನರ್ಗ್ಗಾವುಂಡ [ಯ್ಯ] ಚಾಳುಕ್ಯವಿ-
11 ಕ್ರಮಂ ಮಾವತ್ಸರದೆನೆಯ ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞತೈವತ್ಸರದ ಚೈತ್ರ ಶುದ್ಧ ಪಾಡಿ
12 ವ ಆದಿತ್ಯವಾರದಂದು ತಿಳವಳ್ಳಿ ಯುಕ್ತವಸಟ್ಟಿ ಕಂಜಯನ ಮಲ್ಲಿಸೆಟ್ಟಿ ದೋ
13 ಣಿಯಕಿಸೆಟ್ಟಿ ಕಯೊಂತಿಕೇತಿಸೆಟ್ಟಿ ಕಾಯಮಿತಿಸೆಟ್ಟಿ-
14 ದ್ವಳ್ಳ ಮಲಸ್ಥಾನದೇವ ದೇವರಿಗೆ ಧಮ್ಮದ ಪೇರ್ವಣಿಯ ವಿಸವೊಂದು ನೊತ್ತರಾಜ
15 ಸಿಂದಣಮುಂ ಉಗುರ ಮನುಮಟ್ಟಾರೂಂ ಬಟ್ಟ ದರ್ಶನಂ ಪಣವೊಂದು ಹನ್ನವನಿ-
16 ಗ ಸಿಂಗಣನು ನೈನ್ನೂಜ ನಾರೂಮಿಲ್ಲು ಬಟ್ಟಿ ಧಮ್ಮದ ಗಾತ್ರಕ್ಕೆ ಯೊಂ-
17 ದು ಹೇಜೂ ನವದ [ದಿ]ಷ್ಟಿ ಧಮ್ಮದಂ ಪ್ರತಿಯಾಗಿನಿಂ ವಾರಣಾಸಿ
18 ಕುರುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಮೊಲು ಸಾಸಿರ್ವ್ವ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರ್ಗೆ = ಸಾವಿರ ಕಪಿಲೆಯ
19 ನುಭಯ ಮುಖವನಿಕ್ಕಿದ ಫಲಮಕ್ಕುವ ಈ ಧಮ್ಮದನ ವಳದವಂಗೆ ವಾರಣಾ-
20 ಸಿ ಕುರುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದೊಳು ಸಾಸಿರ್ವ್ವ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರುಮಂ ಸಾವಿರ ಕಪಿಲೆ-
21 ಯಮಂ ನಳಿದ ಪಞ್ಚಮಹಾಪಾತಕಕ್ಕುವಂ || ಸ್ವದತ್ತಂ ಪರ-
22 ದತ್ತಂ ವಾ ಯೋ ಹರೇತಿ ವಸುಂಧರಾ | ಷಷ್ಟಿರ್ವವರ್ಷ ಸಹ-
23 [ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ] ಯಾಂ ಜಾಯಂತೇ ಕ್ರಿಮಿ || ರಾಮೋತ್ಸರ
24 ಪಂಡಿತರಿಲ್ಲದಿಕಾರಗಳ ||

The details of date are:- Chalukya Vikrama year 32, Sarvajit, Chaitra, su. Padiva, Sunday. Sarvajit fell in Saka 1029 which was Ch. Vik. year 31.
In this year the given tithi occurred on a Monday, (not Sunday) whereas for the next year i.e. Saka 1030, Sarvadharin which corresponded to Ch. Vik. year 32, the details regularly corresponded to Sunday, March 15, A. D. 1108. The cyclic year is evidently an expired one.
I piece
II piece
[Footnote 1] The stone is broken away after this.

ಚಾಳುಕ್ಯಾಭರಣ ಶ್ರೀ ಮತ್ರಿಭುವನಮಲ್ಲದೇವ ವಿಜಯರಾಜ್ಯ ಮುತ್ತರಾಜ್ಯ ಮುಕ್ತ4 ರೋತ್ತರಾಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿ ಪ್ರವರ್ದ್ಧಮಾನ ಮಾಚಂದ್ರಾರ್ಕ ತಾರಂಬರಂ ಸಲ್ವತ್ತೆ || ತತ್ಯಾದಪದ್ಮೋಪಜೀವಿ ||5 ಶ್ರೀ ಮತ್ಕದಂಬವಂಶಕಲಶೋದ್ಭವನಾದ ಹಿಮಾಂಶು ರಾಜ್ಯಲಕ್ಷ್ಮೀ ಭಾಜಿತಪ್ರಮದಿ-ನುಯಿಸಿದಂ ಬಲದೀ-6 ಮಖಿಯೊಳ್ ಕೀರ್ತಿಕರಣದಿಂ ಶೈಲಪ್ರಪಂ || ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷ ಧರ್ಮ್ಮತೇಜನು ಸುಜ್ಞಂ ಪ್ರಿಪಾಗು-ಗಣ್ಯ ಸೂಜಿ ತಿತೃ-7 ಣ್ಯಂ ಸತ್ಯರಾಧೇಯಂ ಸಮರಸಿನಾಧಿಕ್ಯಂ ನಭಮಾನದಾನಿ ತೈಲಪಭೂಪಾಲ || ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಸಮಸ್ತ [ಗಂ] ತ ಪಂಚಮಹಾ-8 ಬ್ಬ ಮಹಾಮಂಡಳೇಶ್ವರ ಕದಂಬನ ಪುವನಾದಿತ್ಯಂ ಜಯನ್ನಿ [ಮ] ಧುಕೇಶ್ವರ ಲಬ್ಧವರಪ್ರಸಾದಂ ಮಿಗ ಮ-9 ಣಾಮೋದಂ ತ್ರಿಭುವನಕೃತ್ಯ ಸಂಭವ ಚತುರಾಸೀತಿ ನಗರದೇವಿತಂ ಲಲಾಟಲೋಚನಚತುರ್ಭುಜ ಜಗದ್ದಿತಾ-10 ಷ್ಟ [ದ*] ರಾಜ್ಯಮೋದೇದೀಕ್ಷಿತನಂ ಹಿಮವದಿ ರೇಂದ್ರಸಿಖರಸಂಸ್ಥಾಪಿತಸ್ಫಟಿಕ ಶಿಲಾಸ್ತಂಭ ಬದ್ಧ ಮದನ11 ಮಯೂರವಾರ್ಮಣ ಕಾದಂಬ ಚಕ್ರಮ್ಮಯರಮವ್ಯ ಮಹಾಮಹೀಪಾಲ ಕುಳಭೂಷಣಂಪೇಮ್ಮ್ಯತ್ಕೃತಿಯುಕ್ತ12 ನಿಗೀರ್ವ್ಯಾಸಂ ಸಾಂಬ್ರಾಜೇಂದ್ರ ಧ್ವಜನಿರಾಜಮಾನ ಮಾನಸೋತ್ಸಂಗ ಸಿಂಗಾಲಂಘನದತ್ತಾತ್ರಿ ಕಾಂಚನ ಸಮರ ಜಯಕಾರ-13 ಣಂ ಕದಂಬಾಭರಣಂ ಮಳಿಕ್ಯಾರ ಘಟ್ಟ ಪ್ರತಾಸ ಮಾತ್ರ್ಯಂಣಂ ನಾಮಾದಿಪರಸ್ಕೃಸಹಿತ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ನ ಹಾಮಣ್ಣ-14 ಳೇಶ್ವರಂ ತೈಲಪದೇವರ್ ಬನವಾಸಿ ಪನ್ನಿಚ್ಛಾ [ಣ*] ಸಿರವಮಂ ಪಾಸನಂಗಲ್ಲ-ಯಿತ್ಯಾದ್ಯುಮಂ ಸುಖ ಸಂಕಥಾವಿನೋದದಿಂ ರಾ-15 ಜ್ಯಂ [ಗೈ] ಯುತ್ತುಮಿರೇ || ತತ್ರಾದಪದ್ಮೋಪಜೀವಿ || ಗಂಗಕುಳವೆಂಬ ದುಗುದೊಲಂಗಿತಹೋಗ್ನ ಸಿದ [ತವೇ] ದರಸಿ-16 ದ ಪೋತ್ರಂಗೆಂ ಬಳಿಕಿಕ್ಕ ಸನಗುಣ ಸಂಗತದನ್ಯೋಜಿ ವಿಜ ನೆಗ್ಗಿದಂ ಧರೆಯೊಳ್ ||ಅನಗನ ಪೆಗ್ಗಡ ಮಾ-17 ತೇನೋ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೂರ್ತಿ ಶಿವಪದಭೂಷಣಂ ಸತುನವಂತರ ಬಡಗೊಮಟನವಿತತ ಕೀ-ರ್ತಿಯುಳ್ಳಂ ಮಿಕ್ಕಂ ||18 ಮಿಕ್ಕಂ ಸಮಸ್ತಗುಣಗಳಂ ಪರದೈವ್ಯೇನಾದೊಡಂ ತಾಂ ಕೊಳ್ದಂ ಕದಂಬ್ಯನಿಸಾ-ಪ್ಯ್ವ್ಯಕಂ ಶಿವಪಾದಯುವಗಂ19 ಪೂಜಸಲವ್ಯಂ || ಈಳವಳಿಯೊಡನೆ ಬಳಿಕೊಂಗುಳಕೆಟ್ಟಂ ಸೆಟ್ಟಿ ಗುಟ್ಟನಿದ್ದ ಹಸು-ಬೆಯುನೆ ||20 ಮಿಲ್ಲಿ ಸಕ್ಕೆಯ ಬಳವಗನ ತನ್ನ ಯೊಂಬರವರುನಪಲಿರೆರು || ಅನ್ನೇನಸಿದ ಪ್ರಭುವಿಭವದಗುನ್ನಿ[ಯೊಳ್]21 ಸಾಯಕೀಯದೇಶಕ ಮನವನನ್ನಗುನು ಮಿಲ್ಡಿಸೀಟಿಗಂ ತಾಂ ತವ್ಯ್ಯಂ ನಾಸಪ್ಯ್-ನಾ ನಾಯ್ಮುಕ್22 ರೂಪಿನ ಮುನೆ ವಿನಯದ ಗೌರವದ ಧಮ್ಮ್ಯದಗಾರಮನೆ ಸನ್ಯನುತ ಗೋತ್ರದ ಕಳತ್ರಕ23 ರೋಜೀರುಚೀ ನಾಯಿನುಮ್ಮ || ಅನ್ನು ತಮ್ವ್ಯ್ವರುನು ಸನ್ನಿಹ ಸಹದರಂಗಳ್ಗಾ[ಗ]24 ಮುಪ್ಪಿನದಪ್ಪ ವದಪ್ಪಾಣ್ನೆಗಂ ಮದೋದಿವ್ಯ್ಗ್ಗಗಗಳಕುರೂರುಂ ಮ .25 ವದಮ್ವ್ಯ್- ಪಾಲ್ಕ್ಯ್ಣಿಗೆ ಯುದ್ಧಕ್ಕರಾಣಿ ನ .26 ಗಪ್ಪುಕ್ಕೀಯುಂ ಮಾಡಿದರುದನ್ನೇ,ಮುಲ27 ಆನ್ನು ತ್ರಿಕುಟಮಣಾ ದೇವಗೃಹ [ಗ]28 ಸಟೋ೯ಕ್ಕಮೆನುತ್ತಿಮಿಣಿ ಗುಡಿಗಿಣಿ 329 ಪರಮತಪ್ಯ್-ಜ್ಞಾನ ಸವ್ವ್ಯಜ್ಞಾ[ತಾ]30 ಲಕುಳೇಶನೇಶಂತೆ ತಾಂ ವ31 [ಹೀ]ಶ್ವರಪ್ಪು ವಿಮಲಶಕ್ತಿಪದ್ಯ್-32 ಯುತಿ ಮಾರ್ಗ್ಗಳ ಫೇ .33 ಣಿ ಜೇಲಿಗಂ

cells.language: Kannada and Sanskrit
cells.remarks: Slab standing inside near the compound wall of the Mamletdar's office. This is a damaged fragmentary inscription belonging to the reign of Tribhuvanamalla-dēva (Vikramāditya VI). It introduces the Sagara- vamsa in which were born Jayakesin, his son Indrakesin and the latter's son Jayakesin. A certain Mahāsāmanta (name lost) born of the Maṇalera lineage with the lion crest is referred to as the governor. As the record is mutilated nothing further can be made out of it. The Sagara family and Maṇalera are mentioned in the Ātkūr inscription of Rāshtrakūṭa Krishna III (Ep. Ind. Vol. VI, p. 53). I Section II Section 382
cells.text_original:
1 The inscription is indifferently worded.
1 * ನಮಸ್ಸುಂಗ ಸಿರಕ್ಕಂಜಿ ಚೆಂಜೇ ಣಮರವ ಚಾ .
2 ಮೂಲಸ್ಥಂಭಾಯ ಸಂಭವೇ || ಗಣಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ್ [.]
3 ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಭುವನಾಶ್ರಯ ಶ್ರೀ ಪೃಥ್ವೀವಲ್ಲಭ ಮಹಾರಾಜಾ .
4 ರಮೇಶ್ವರ ಪರಮಭಟ್ಟಾರಕಂ ಸತ್ಯಾಶ್ರಯಕುಳತಿ .
5 ಕಾವ್ಯಭರಣಂ ಶ್ರೀಮತ್ತ್ರಿ ಭುವನಮಲ್ಲದೇವದ ನಿಜ .
6 . ರಾಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿ ಪುನರ್ಧ್ಮ್ಯಮಾನವನಾ ಚಂದ್ರಾಕ್ಕ್ಯ್-ತಾರಂ
7 . ರೇ || ತತ್ಪಾದ ಸದ್ವೇಣ್ಯಪೂಜಾ || ನಗರವಂಶದೊಳ್
8 . ನೆಗಲ್ಬು ದನೆ ಜಯುಕೇಸಿಶೂಯಾತನ ಸುತಂ ನೆಗಲ್ಬುದೃಕ್ಚೇಸಿಂಯಾ .
9 . ತನಯಂ ಜಯುತಕೇಸಿಎನ್ಯ್-ದೆ ಪೋಗಳ್ಕ
10 . ನಣ್ಣಾರಸಂ ಸಮುಧಿಕ ಪಂಚಮಹಾಸಬ್ದ ಮಹಾ .
11 . ಮಣಿ [ಅ] ರಾಗಸ್ಯದ ಪ್ರಸಂತ ಸಿಂಹಲಾಂಚನ [ಪ್ರು]
12 . ಪ್ರಚಣ್ಣಮ್ಮಣ್ಕಾರು[ಬ]ಣ್ಣೆಗ ದೋದ್ಧಣ್ಣಂ ಸ .
13 . ದಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ ಸಹಿತಂ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ನ ಹಾಸಮಂತಾಧಿ .
14 . ಗಣ . ಸುಖದಿನಾಳ್ದರಸು .
15 . ಳೆಗೀ .
1 Broken away after this.

cells.remarks: Slab standing before the Kalmēśvara Temple. This inscription belongs to the reign of Jagadēkamalladēva (II) and introduces his subordinate Mahāpradhāna, Daṇḍanāyaka Kēśimayya as ruling over the Eraḍaruṇūru (the two six hundred) division. In Kuntala was Belvola in which was included the town Risisingapura also called Pirisingi in l. 13. The Six Gauḍas of Pirisingi are then extolled. On the date specified in ll. 18 f. Kāvaṇagaḍa of Tolaha-kuḷa is stated to have granted two mattar of land for worship and repairs in the temple of Grāmēśvaradēva, into the hands of āchārya Rudra-Śaktidēva. Similarly Mūliga Chiyalagaṇḍa, Tippagaṇḍa of Tolapakula, Bōsigāvuṇḍa of the Arindara-kuḷa, Padmagaṇuḍa and Mūliga Bammagaṇḍa are also stated to have severally endowed lands for the same temple. The recipient of the gifts was Rudra-Śaktidēva. Sōri-gāvuṇḍi, wife of Sāguḷada Rāji- gāvuṇḍa, a member of the Six Gauḍas gave land for a local tank. The inscription was composed (pēldaru) by Kalidēva-Paṇḍita, lay- disciple (gudda) of Bhuvanachandra-Siddhāntadēva and engraved by Rūvārichakravartin Sumatōja. [Footnote 1] Broken away after this. The details of date are: Jagadekamalladeva year 11, Vibha[va], Pushya, su. 10, Monday, Sankramana and Vyatipata. They are irregular. If Monday (Sōmavāra) is a mistake for Wednesday (Saumya-vāra), the date would correspond to Wednesday, December 22, A. D. 1148. But the Sankramana (i. e. the Makara-Sankramana) occurred two days later i. e. Friday, December 24, A. text.remarks:
Slab standing before the Kalmēśvara Temple.
This inscription belongs to the reign of Jagadēkamalladēva (II) and
introduces his subordinate Mahāpradhāna, Daṇḍanāyaka Kēśimayya as
ruling over the Eraḍaruṇūru (the two six hundred) division. In Kuntala
was Belvola in which was included the town Risisingapura also called
Pirisingi in l. 13. The Six Gauḍas of Pirisingi are then extolled. On
the date specified in ll. 18 f. Kāvaṇagaḍa of Tolaha-kuḷa is stated to have
granted two mattar of land for worship and repairs in the temple of
Grāmēśvaradēva, into the hands of āchārya Rudra-Śaktidēva. Similarly
Mūliga Chiyalagaṇḍa, Tippagaṇḍa of Tolapakula, Bōsigāvuṇḍa of the
Arindara-kuḷa, Padmagaṇuḍa and Mūliga Bammagaṇḍa are also stated to
have severally endowed lands for the same temple. The recipient of the
gifts was Rudra-Śaktidēva. Sōri-gāvuṇḍi, wife of Sāguḷada Rāji-
gāvuṇḍa, a member of the Six Gauḍas gave land for a local tank.
The inscription was composed (pēldaru) by Kalidēva-Paṇḍita, lay-
disciple (gudda) of Bhuvanachandra-Siddhāntadēva and engraved by
Rūvārichakravartin Sumatōja.
[Footnote 1] Broken away after this.
The details of date are: Jagadekamalladeva year 11, Vibha[va],
Pushya, su. 10, Monday, Sankramana and Vyatipata. They are irregular.
If Monday (Sōmavāra) is a mistake for Wednesday (Saumya-vāra), the
date would correspond to Wednesday, December 22, A. D. 1148. But
the Sankramana (i. e. the Makara-Sankramana) occurred two days later
i. e. Friday, December 24, A. D. 1148.

cells.remarks: Slab standing in Kalamma temple. After invocation to Sambhu and the Boar-incarnation of Vishnu, the record refers itself to the reign of Tribhuvanamalla Vira-Somesvara (IV), and in a number of verses gives a mythological account of the village of Risyasringa in Kolanur-Thirty division (Kampana) which was included in Beluvola of the Kuntala country. The village is stated to have been rendered sacred on account of the temples of Ramesvara, Lakshmanesvara and Hanmantesvara installed there by Sri-Rama and Lakshmana who after destroying the demons headed by Ravana camped at the hermitage of Risyasringa on their way to Ayodhya. These are introduced the six Gaundas and the illustrious Habbeya-Nayaka of the fourth caste who was the Mahaprabhu of Risyasringa. His genealogy is follows:- (i) Bacha-Nayaka m. Bachiyakka (ii) Hiriya-Habbeya-Nayaka m. Jondiyakka | Bacha Huli, m. Balliyakka. Habbeya-Nayaka m. (i) Malliyakka-Nayakiti, d. of Chatta-Gavunda. (ii) Kalavve. Bachayya The family deity of Habbeya is given as Lila-Bhairavadeva. Habbeya-Nayaka listened to the sermons on the excellence of installing the images of Isvara and the merit accruing therefrom and constructed in stone the temples of Habbesvara and Prasanna-Bhairava at Risyasringa. On the date specified in lines 72-73, he granted four mattur of land after purchasing it from Tajiya Chatta Gavunda, son of Acha-Gavunda in the presence of the eight Hittus and the five matha-sthana (bodies), for worship, offerings and renovations in the temple of Habbesvara. The gift was entrusted to Vamasaktideva, the acharya of the temple. Chatta-gavunda granted, on this occasion, one mattur of land for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple. Mallave, the senior Nayakiti (hiriya-nayakiti) of Habbeya-Nayaka is stated to have built the temple of Umamahesvara in the precincts of the Habbesvara temple and endowed one mattur for it. Various gifts of land by certain Gavundas and other individuals are registered. Lines 83-91 describe the several trade guilds who assembled in Hirisinge at the temple as Bayisanige and exempted for all times to come, the levy of taxes on the loads of provisions to be carried by sixty-five oxen. The Nakharas also gave a specified money and articles of worship for conducting the festival of chaitra and pavitra in the Habbesvara temple. The following merchant guilds are mentioned:- The five hundred Svamins of Ayyahole (their lineage and deities described), the Settis, the Settiguttas of the eight towns in the two six-hundred districts, the Mummuridandas of all the places, the Settiguttas of the three thousand and four towns, all the Ubhaya-Nanadesigal, Birudas, Biravanigas, Gavares, Gatrigas, the fifty okkals and the Nakharas. In lines 91-93, a gift of one haga on each horse-load is registered for the Habbesvara temple of Biravaniga-Habbeya-Nayaka, by the nana. [Kannada original] [English translation, Gemini-rendered, verify] The Kennala (land) to the Ganges, the cow-gift to Kurukshetra. The sin-destroyer, the Gumaba, the district, the Nigodadagalu. The architect, the beautiful-faced Kannaraka. desa merchants of Lala and Maleyala, headed by Mahavadda-Vyavahari Siri Kumara-Nayaka, Ravi-Nayaka and other Nayakas, Mana- vala-setti, Elanambi-setti, Maleyachi-setti and Kondanabisetti who had assembled at Hirisingi at Mahanadu. It is interesting to note that Hirisingi had attracted merchants from all over the Tamil and Telugu countries besides those in Karnataka. The functions and jurisdiction of these various bodies of commerce are however not clear. The central chamber of commerce which had its seat at Ayyavole had received inspi- ration from the goddess Bhagavatidevi and were descended from Bala- deva, Vasudeva Khandali and Mulabhadra. These deities are Jain. This shows that the commerce of the Deccan and South India was captured by the Jains in the early period. The record was composed by the illustrious poet Sajjana-tilaka in modern Kannada (posa-gannada) and Satoja, grandson of Chandoja who was the employer of sculptors (ruvari-chakravartin) engraved it. This whose proper name is not disclosed, must have been a poet of high order as is borne out by the poems of the inscription. The details of date are: Saka 1108, Visvavasu, Pushya, Paurnamase, Monday, Uttarayana-Sankramana, Vyatipata. They are not quite regular. The Uttarayana-Sankramana occurred on Tuesday, December 24, A. D. 1185, whereas the other details fell on Monday, January 6, record. The gift might have been made on the day of Sankranti and put on stone on January 6, A. D. 1186. 46 382 47

After invocation to Sambhu and the Boar-incarnation of Vishnu, the record refers itself to the reign of Tribhuvanamalla Vira-Somesvara (IV), and in a number of verses gives a mythological account of the village of Risyasringa in Kolanur-Thirty division (Kampana) which was included in Beluvola of the Kuntala country. The village is stated to have been rendered sacred on account of the temples of Ramesvara, Lakshmanesvara and Hanmantesvara installed there by Sri-Rama and Lakshmana who after destroying the demons headed by Ravana camped at the hermitage of Risyasringa on their way to Ayodhya. These are introduced the six Gaundas and the illustrious Habbeya-Nayaka of the fourth caste who was the Mahaprabhu of Risyasringa. His genealogy is follows:-
(i) Bacha-Nayaka
m. Bachiyakka
(ii) Hiriya-Habbeya-Nayaka
m. Jondiyakka
|
Bacha Huli,
m. Balliyakka.
Habbeya-Nayaka
m. (i) Malliyakka-Nayakiti, d. of Chatta-Gavunda.
(ii) Kalavve.
Bachayya
The family deity of Habbeya is given as Lila-Bhairavadeva. Habbeya-Nayaka listened to the sermons on the excellence of installing the images of Isvara and the merit accruing therefrom and constructed in stone the temples of Habbesvara and Prasanna-Bhairava at Risyasringa. On the date specified in lines 72-73, he granted four mattur of land after purchasing it from Tajiya Chatta Gavunda, son of Acha-Gavunda in the presence of the eight Hittus and the five matha-sthana (bodies), for worship, offerings and renovations in the temple of Habbesvara. The gift was entrusted to Vamasaktideva, the acharya of the temple. Chatta-gavunda granted, on this occasion, one mattur of land for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple. Mallave, the senior Nayakiti (hiriya-nayakiti) of Habbeya-Nayaka is stated to have built the temple of Umamahesvara in the precincts of the Habbesvara temple and endowed one mattur for it. Various gifts of land by certain Gavundas and other individuals are registered.
Lines 83-91 describe the several trade guilds who assembled in Hirisinge at the temple as Bayisanige and exempted for all times to come, the levy of taxes on the loads of provisions to be carried by sixty-five oxen. The Nakharas also gave a specified money and articles of worship for conducting the festival of chaitra and pavitra in the Habbesvara temple. The following merchant guilds are mentioned:- The five hundred Svamins of Ayyahole (their lineage and deities described), the Settis, the Settiguttas of the eight towns in the two six-hundred districts, the Mummuridandas of all the places, the Settiguttas of the three thousand and four towns, all the Ubhaya-Nanadesigal, Birudas, Biravanigas, Gavares, Gatrigas, the fifty okkals and the Nakharas.
In lines 91-93, a gift of one haga on each horse-load is registered for the Habbesvara temple of Biravaniga-Habbeya-Nayaka, by the nana.
[Kannada original]
[English translation, Gemini-rendered, verify]
The Kennala (land) to the Ganges, the cow-gift to Kurukshetra.
The sin-destroyer, the Gumaba, the district, the Nigodadagalu.
The architect, the beautiful-faced Kannaraka.
desa merchants of Lala and Maleyala, headed by Mahavadda-Vyavahari
Siri Kumara-Nayaka, Ravi-Nayaka and other Nayakas, Mana-
vala-setti, Elanambi-setti, Maleyachi-setti and Kondanabisetti who
had assembled at Hirisingi at Mahanadu. It is interesting to note that
Hirisingi had attracted merchants from all over the Tamil and Telugu
countries besides those in Karnataka. The functions and jurisdiction of
these various bodies of commerce are however not clear. The central
chamber of commerce which had its seat at Ayyavole had received inspi-
ration from the goddess Bhagavatidevi and were descended from Bala-
deva, Vasudeva Khandali and Mulabhadra. These deities are Jain.
This shows that the commerce of the Deccan and South India was
captured by the Jains in the early period.
The record was composed by the illustrious poet Sajjana-tilaka in
modern Kannada (posa-gannada) and Satoja, grandson of Chandoja
who was the employer of sculptors (ruvari-chakravartin) engraved it.
This whose proper name is not disclosed, must have been a
poet of high order as is borne out by the poems of the inscription.
The details of date are: Saka 1108, Visvavasu, Pushya, Paurnamase,
Monday, Uttarayana-Sankramana, Vyatipata. They are not quite
regular. The Uttarayana-Sankramana occurred on Tuesday, December
24, A. D. 1185, whereas the other details fell on Monday, January 6,
record. The gift might have been made on the day of Sankranti and
put on stone on January 6, A. D. 1186.

|| ದ್ವಿಜಗೀಂದ್ರಂರಾಜ್ಯ ಕುಲದೆಯ್ಯನೆ-ನುತ್ತೆಅಗಳು ಪ್ರಜಜ್ಞ ಮಾವನಸಿನವಪೇಂದ್ರಾದಿಗಳು ವಲಂಪಿಪೊಲುವದೇಗಲುಫಣೇಂದ್ರ-5 ರುಷ್ಟವದಜೇಲು ಜಗತ್ರಯವದಿನಸದಧಿಕ ಪ್ರಸನ್ನಲಕ್ಷ್ಮೀದವನಾರಾದಿ ಕಡಗಹೆಚ್ಚಿಯನಾಯಕನಕೃತ್ತಾತ್ಮಕಂ || ಬಲದಿಂ ಪ್ರವದ್ಧಮಾನಚಂದ್ರಾರ್ಕ ತಾರಾ-ಬರಂ ಸಲ್ಲುತ್ತಿಮರೆ ||8 ಭಾಳಾಕ್ಷಾದ್ವಿತಿ ಬಡವಾಗಿ ಗೆ ಜಟಾಜೂಟಂ ಪ್ರವಾಳಕ ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಕಾರ್ಮದಮಹಿಕೋಟಿಗೇ ಕರೋಟಿಟಮಾಲಿ ಶೇಪಾಲಗಾಭೀಳಧ್ಯಾ ನಮುದಿನಾ ಫೂಣಿಕೇಶೀಶಯಾ-ಗಲು ಪುಣ್ಯಲಕ್ಷ್ಮೀದವ ರಥ ಲೀಲಾ9 ಕೃತಿಪೊಲು ಮೇಲಂ ಮೇಲೆನಿಪು-12 ದೆಂ ಗಣಪಂ || ಅಧ್ವಜದಿಯಂ || ಶ್ರೀಮಲ್ಲ ನರೇಂದ್ರಂ ಸುಮನೇನೋಮಾಳದ ಭಾಸಿಬಹಳಾಲಾಕೀಶ್ವರಯೆಂಬೆ ಮಯ್ಯಿ ಇಣೇಣಿಯಾದಲಾಮಸಿಲೆಯ ಕುಂತಳಕ್ಕೆಕುಂತಳದೇಶದೊಳು || ಇತ್ತೆ-13 ಸಿ || ಸುರುಚಿರ ಕುಂತಳದ ಕಳೊಉದ್ಧ ಸುವರ್ಣಾ ಗಮಿನತ ರತ್ನನ ಶಾಖಾವಾಕೀಕೃತವನಾಲಕಯ್ಯು ಲಾಟಾಂತಾಂತಿಕ ವಿತ್ತಿ ಕೃತ್ಯಂಗಂಗಮಂ ||15 ಆ ಸ್ಥಳದಾದಿ ಪ್ರಪಂಚವೇತಂದೊಡನೆ || ತಮವನವೃದ್ದಿ ಕೃತ್ಯದಧಿ ಕೃತ್ಯಾಧಿಯಾಮಣು ಭುವನಂ ಪೂರ್ವಾಪರ ವಾದ್ರಿಯಾಣೆ ನಿಜ ವಿಸ್ತಾರಕೃತಿವನೀಜಾ ಹಿಮವದಾದಿ ವೃಂದಾಧರಗಣಾಧರಕಂ ||16 ರಿಕ್ಷಿಶೃಂಗಬ್ರತೀಶ್ವರಗಾಯಿತಕಳ್ಯಯವಂತದೇವನಳಯಂ ಕಿಸ್ಮಥದಂ ಬದ್ಧ ಸೆಲು || ಆನಗಪತಿಯು ಜಗಂತುತ ಸಾನುವಿನೊಳು ಕಂದಮೂಲಫಲಸಂಕಲಂ18 ದೋಳು ಭುನತ ವಿಭಾಂಢಕ ಬದಿ ತಾನಿಪ್ಪಂ ಸಕಳವೇದವೇದಾಂಗದೊಳು || ಮೃಗಗಣಸರಿಶೃಪ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಳ್ಳ ನಿಸರ್ಗ್ಯನಿವಂ ತೌಜಿನಾ ಸಾನುವಿನೊಳು ಚರಿಯುಪಿನೆ-ಲಾಜ್ಞೆಗ ಸಾಹತಿನಿ ನೋರ್ತಾವ್ಯಭಾಂಢಕ ಮುನಿಪೊಳು || ವಿಕಾ-19 ತ್ತಿ ನಿಃಸಂಹಂ ಶಾಂತಾಕರನೊನೆ ಕಣಿದೆ ನೆಗಳ್ಳ ಕೈಸಂಖ್ಯಕೃತಾಕ್ಷ್ಯಯ್ಯದೊಲ್ಲ ಫಲಾಕಾಂಕ್ಷೆಯುಳದು ತಮ್ಯನೀಯಂ ನೆಗಳ್ಳ || ಸ್ಯಾನಾಕತಾದಿ ವಿಭಾಂಢಕಾನ ನಗ-ದೊಳದೊಂದು ತೀರ್ಥಕಲ್ಪದಿದರತ ನಳಿನಿಯೊಳ್ಗ ತಪನಿ-20 ಧಾಮಮನ್ನೇಶಿಯನಾ ಮುನಿಣದೊಂ ಕಂದಂ || ಕಾಳೇದನಡೆನೆ || ಅಶ್ಯಕತತ್ತ್ವನಾಜೇತೃಕಳ್ಯಯೊ] ಪವನಸಿನಿ ಪೂಜಾಪೂಣ್ಯವಶಕೃತ್ಯನಾಗಿ ನಾನಾಕೃತಮುವಾಂ-ಸಿನತವ ದಳವೊಲಿಸಂಖದಂ21 ನಾಂತಂ || ಮರೆದಿಡಿಯಾಜ್ಞಾಯಿಸೆ ಮುನಿಪದರವಿಯಾನಮೋಹಪಾವಿಜ್ಯಾವ್ಯಥಜಣಿದಾ ಮರೆದಿಟ್ಟು ಗರ್ಭದಿನದತಪದಿನೆನ್ನೊಂ || ಕುಮಾರಕಂ ಕೃ[ಅ]ಗಯತಂ || ಆಗಣಂ || ಪುರುಕಾಳಾದ ರೊಪಂ ಮದರಿಂ-22 ಡೆಂ ಕಾಳೇದಿನಡೆನೆ ಯಮ ಮರೆದಿಟ್ಟು ಕೃತಿಯ ರೂಪಂ ತಳೇದಂಬರಕ್ಕೆ ಪಾಜದು(ದು)ನಿಜ ನಿವಾಸಮನೆದ್ದು ಉಣ || ಅದೆಂತೊಡೊಡೆ ಮಂಜುಭಿನಸೇಯೊಂಬಟ್ಟ ರಸಯೊಮ್ಮ್ಯರಾಗಿಣಂ ರಾಗಾಂಧಯಾಗಿ ಕೃಗೊಯಿತು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ-23 ಹೀಲಯುನ್ನನೊಗೆಯುತ್ತಿದ್ದುದದಳಿಯದು ತಂದ ಸನಾಗತಳಯರ, ಸಾರಣ್ಯ ಪೂಜತವಶನಿನಾ ಕೃಗೊಯಂ ಶ್ರೀಗಯಂ ಸೋಕುವಂತ ಸೋಣಿತ ಕುದುನಗುಬ್ಬಿನ ಚಾಗಿಯನಲ್ಲ ಭೀತಿಯಂ ಶಿರಸಿನೆ ಕಾವ ದೇವನಿನಾಲವಳಿಯಂ ಪೋಗಲ್ಪುದು ದೊಲ್ಲಲು ಸಾಕ್ಷಿಕಥಾನನಂ ನೆಗಳ್ಳ ಹಚ್ಚೆಯನಾಯಕನಂಗುಣಾತ್ಮನಂ || ಇಂತೇನಿಸಿ || ಸೈನ್ಯ ಸಮಸ್ತ ನಾಯಕ ಮಸ್ಕಣ್ಯ-62 ಸ್ವನಸ್ತಮನೆಪಾಯದ ರಣಾಕಠಿನೋತ್ಸವದ || ಸಹಸ್ರಮಿನದೊಡಮದೇವೀರಚರಿತಕಥಾವಿನೋದ || ಭಕ್ತಿಪ್ರಧಾನದಾನಕಾನಿನ || ವಿಜಯಾಗಣಾವಲ್ಲಭಂ ಭಯತೋಜದಮಲಗುಣಂ | ಚಾಪಾಗಮದತ್ತೇನಕಶರಣಪರಿಪಾಲನಭ್ಯಾ-63 ಣ || ವೈರಿಜಧಧರಭುಜಂ ಸುಜನಜನಮನೋರಂಜನಂ | ಶರಣಾಗತವಜ್ರಪಂಜರಂವೈರಿರಾಯದಳಕಂಠಂ ಮಟ್ಟಿನಿದಾನದೊಳ್ ಸಿದ್ಧಂ ನುಡಿದ ದುಷ್ಟನಾಯಕನ ಸತ್ಯ-ಲ್ಯಂ ಮುಜಾಜೊಟ್ಟೆಯುಮಂಟೆಯ್ಯನಾದಿಸುವ ಬಿರುದನಾಯಕ ಶಿರದಿನಪ್ಪಂ ಬಿಡಿ-ಚ್ಚುರ್ವ ಜಪ-64 [ಅ]ನಾಯಕ ಹೃದಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಭೀತನಾಯಕನಂ ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ ಸತ್ಯರಾಧೆಯ ಸಾಹಸವೈನೆ-ತೀಯ || ಸಕಳ ದಿಜದವಜಭುಜಕಂಠನೊಡನೆಗಿರಿದಿಗ್ವಿದ್ಯಾನಿಧಿ ದ್ರೇಂದ್ರನತಮಣಿಮಕುಟಮಕುಟ್ಯಸಂಘಟಿತ || ತಥಾವದೀಪಾಲಾಂತ್ರಿ-65 ತ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಮೂಲೀಲಾನೇತಕ ರುದ್ರಾವತಾರ @ ವೀರಭಿ ರದೇವನಿದ್ದ @ ಪ್ರಸಾದದರಾಧಕಂ ಪರಮ[ಂ]ದಳ ಸೂಜಿಕಾರ್ಯಪ್ಪ ಶ್ರೀಮತು ಹಚ್ಚೆಯನಾಯಕಂನಿಜ ಭುಜಬಲೋಪಾರ್ಜಿತ ಸಂಪತ್ತಿಯುಂ ಸುದಿನದನಭಾಸುತ್ರಿದ್ಯೊಂ ದೇವಂತಾನನ-66 ಹಾಯಕನಾನದವಜಂ ಪುರಾತನರತ್ನಸಹಾಯಕರದ || ಕಥಾಪಸಂಚಿತಗಳ್ಳನವರಂಕುಜುತ್ತು ಹೆಲ್ಲಳ ಶುಭಾಶಿತಂಗಳ್ಳಂ ಕೇಳುತ್ತಿದ್ಧಾನದೊಡನೆ || ನ ತೀ ಕುಲಕೃ-ಮಂ ಯಾತ ಶಾಸನಂ ಲಿಖಿತಾಸಿ ಪಾ ಮಿದ್ಧಮಾವಶ್ಯಕ ಲ-67 ತ್ಮೇ ವೀರಭೋಜ್ಯ ವಸುಂಧರಾ || ಅಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಂ ಪರಿತ್ಯಜ್ಯ ಸಮಸ್ತಂ ಪ್ರತಿಯುತ ಸಾಪ್ರಿಭಿನ್ಯಾ ನಾಸ್ತಿ ಮನ್ಯುಂದಾ ವೀರಭೋಜ್ಯಜಸನಂದರಾ || ಇವು ಮೊದಲಾಗಿನಿಜಪುತ್ರಾಪವಾನಸಾರಗಳ್ಳ ಪಲವು ಶುಭಾಶಿತಂಗಳಂ ಬಲ್ಲನ-68 ಕ್ಕೇಅಳಿ ತಂ ಬಲ್ಲಗೆ || ಬಸವನಾಯಕನೊಡನೆವ್ಯವಭಿಪ್ರಾಯದ ನಂಬುಗೆ ಮನಬಲ್ಲಗಳ್ಳಸಂಪತ್ತಿಗಳ್ಳ ಪುಣ್ಯಮಂ ಮೊದಲಾ ಪುಣ್ಯಕ್ಕೇಳ್ಳಿನುರ ಪುತ್ತಿಯೊ ನೆತ್ತನೋದಲೇನಪೇಲಾ ಪುಣ್ಯದ ಬಲಾದಿಎಲ್ಲಾ ಪುಣ್ಯಂ-69 ಕುಂ ದೊರೆಕೊಳ್ಳಂ ಮತ್ತವೆಲ್ಲಾ ಪ್ರತಿಪೊಗಳಂ ಪ್ರತಿಜ್ಞೆಮಾಡಿದೊಡನಾ ದೇವ್ವಳಹೆಸರೇಕುಯ್ಯಕ್ಕನ ಪುತ್ರಿಯಂ ಮಾಡಿದನನಿತೆನಗಣ್ಯದೇವನಯನ ದೇವದಹೆಸರತನ ಹೆಸರಕ್ಕ್ಯವದೇವನೊಳುಕೊಂಡನ ದಾನ-70 ರು ಕಮ್ಮ್ಯವಪಕ್ಷಕಾ ಕಮ್ಮಶಿಕಾಕಮ್ಮ್ಯಂ [ಗ*] ಳಿಂದೊಂದೆಕ್ಕೆ ಸಹಸ್ರಧಿಕಣ-ದೇವನಾಯನದೊಡಲಶಂ ಬಯಸಿಕೊಳಗಾದದ್ದು ಆ ಹಚ್ಚೇಶ್ವರದೇವದೇವಕಾಯ್ಯ [ಕ] ರ್ತೃವಾಗಿ ಯ-87 ಲ್ಯಾದಿತ್ಯಾಂ ನಾಮಕೃತ್ವಾ ದೇವಗೀ ಭಾಪ್ರತ್ಯಕಂ ಮಾಡಿ ಯಾ ಪುಣ್ಯದಿನದೊಳು ಆವಂತಿ ಪಂಚವನ್ನಿ ಗೆಯದಶತಿಕಲಘುಭಣ್ಯಗೇನ ಹೋದದಂ ಸನ್ಯಾ ಬಾಧೆ ಪಾದಿಹರಾಗಿ ಜಕ್ಕಸಮ್ಮದ್ರ ಪುಣ್ಯಂತ ನಡುವುತು ಬಿಟ್ಟಿ ಎತ್ತಜು ಮುತ್ತ88 [ಅ] ಯ್ಯು || ಮತ್ಸವಾದಿಂ ಹಿಂಸಿಯಿಂ ನಮರಂಗಳ ಹಚ್ಚೇಶ್ವರದೇವ ಕೃತ್ರದಪರ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಪಾದಿಂಗೆ ಪಟ್ಟ ಹಾಣ್ವಂದು | ಪೂತಾರೋಪಣದ ಪರ್ವಕ್ಕೆಪ್ರಕೃತಿಪಾದಿಂಗೆ ಬಿಟ್ಟಿ ಹಾಗೆಹೊಂದು ಯಾ ಸ್ಥಳದೊಳಗೆ ಬಂದ ದೇವದೇವಯಲುಕಾ-89 ಜರಲ್ಲ ಯಾ ದೇವನ ದೇವಕಾಯ್ಯಕೆ ಬಿಟ್ಟಿ ಭಕ್ತಿಲಿಂಗ ಭಕ್ತಿ ಬಲ್ಲಪೊಂದು ಹೇಜಂಗಿಭಕ್ತವದನ | ನಾ ದೇವ ವಿಳಿಯ ನಡವಂಕು ಬಂದ ಗಾತ್ರಗಳೊ ಬಿಟ್ಟಿ ಎಲೆ |ಹೇಜಂಗಿ ನಂಜು ಹೊಜಗಿಯಿತ್ಯು ಯಲ್ಲಿಯಯ್ತಿಕೇಷ್ಟ್ರುಲುಗಳ ದೇವದ90 ನಂದಾವಿಂಗೆ ನಡವಣಾಗಿ ಗಾಣಗಣಸಣಿತಿನಪದಳೊಲು ಹೊಯ್ಯು ಗಾಣಗಳುಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ನೋಡಿಕೊಂಬೊಂತಾಗಿ ಧಾರಣೆಗೆ ಯಿದ್ದ ಸಕಲ | ಱ ಇಂತೀ ಧಮ್ಮಮಣವಗ್ಗಾಫುಂಡಗಳಳುವಮನೆರೆಯ ಮತ್ಸರಂಗಿ ಹಾಣ್ವಂದು [ಹ]91 ರಳ ಮತ್ಸರಂಗಿ ಯದ್ಧವಂ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಟ್ಟ ನೋಡಿಕೊಂದು ಸ್ವಧಮ್ಮ್ಯಾದಿಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾಲಕರು@ || ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ ಸಹಿತಂ ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಮಹಾವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಸಿರಿಕುಮಾರನಾಯಕನಂ ದೇವನಾಯನರು ದೇವಕಾಯ್ಯನರುಂ ಬಲ್ಲಾಳರಾಯರರುಂ92 ಸಂಗನಾಯಕರು ರಾಜದೇವನಾಯನರು ಪಡವನಾಯಕರು ಮಣಾನಾಯಕಲೆ ಎನಬಸಿಟ್ಟಿ ಮಲೆಯಣಶೆಟ್ಟಿ ಕೊಂಡನಬಿಸಿಟ್ಟಿ ಮುಖ್ಯ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಲಾಳಮಲೆಯಾಳನಾನಾದೇಶಿಗಳೊ ಹಿಂಸಿಯಿಂಗಳು ಮಹಾದಾನಂ ಕಳ್ಳುದ್ದು ದೇವನು93 ಹಿರಿಯ ಬಿದದಗಳೊ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಯಸನಾಯ್ಕ ಪುತ್ರಿಕೃಪದ ಪಟ್ಟೆಲ್ಲರ ದೇವಕಾಯ್ಯಕ್ಕೆಕುದುರೆಗೆ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿ ಬಿಟ್ಟಿ ಹಾಗೆಹೊಂದು | @ ಸಾಹಸಂನೊಯ್ಯು ಧಮ್ಮಸೇತುಂನಪಾಲನಾ ಕಾಲೇ ಪಾಲೇ ಪಾಲನೀಯೋ ಭವಂತಿ | ಸರ್ವಾಪೇಕ್ಷಿತಂ94 ಭಾವನಿಃ ಸಾಕ್ಷಿಃ ದೇವದ್ರಾನ್ಯ ಯೋಭೂಯೋವಾ ಯಾಚತೇ ರಾಮಚಂದ್ರ || ಮದ್ಯಂತಜಾಪರಮಪಿತೀಶನವ ಸಾ ಪಾದಪದೇಶತನವ ಸಾ ಭುನಿ ಭೂಮಿಪಾಲನಾ ಯೋಪಾಲಯಂತಿ ಮಮ ಧಮ್ಮ್ಯಾದಂ ಸಮಾ-95 ಸ್ತಂ ತೇಷಾಂ ಮಯಾ ವಿರಚಿತಾಂಜಲೀಕ ಮಧ್ಯಾ || ಬಹುಭಿರ್ವಸುಧಾ ದತ್ತಾರಾಜಭಿಃ ಸಗರಾದಿಭಿಃ ಯಸ್ಯಯಸ್ಯ ಯದಾ ಭೂಮಿಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ತದ ಫಲಂ || ದಾನಂಪಾಲನವತಿ ದಾನಾತ್‌ ಯೋನುಪಾಲನಂ ದಾನಾತ್‌ ಗಮಮಾಪ್ಯೋತಿ96 ಪಾಲನಾದಚ್ಯುತಂ ಪದಂ || ಸ್ಯಾದಾತಂ ಸುಮಹತ್ಸಕ್ಯಂ ದುಃಖಮವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಪಾಲನಂ ದಾನಪಾಲನಯೋರ್ಮಧ್ಯೆ ವರಂ ತೇ ರೇನುಪಾಲನಂ || ಸ್ವದತ್ತ ಪರದತ್ತಂ ವಾ ಯೋಹರೇಹರೇತ ವಸುಂಧರಾ ಷಷ್ಠಿರ್ವಷ ಸಹಸ್ರಾಣಿ ವಿಷ್ಟಾಯಾಂ97 ಜಾಯತೇ ಕ್ರಿಮಿ || ವಿಂಧ್ಯಾವಿಟವೀಷು ತೋಯಾ ಸು ವೃಕ್ಷಕೋಟೀಷು ನಿರಾಶ ಸತ್ವಾಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಜವದ್ಭ್ಯಾಪಹಾರಕ || ಅಸ್ಮಿಕರಣ್ಗಳು ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದೊಳ್ವಂತುನಿವಾರ್ಕಳ98 ವೈವ್ಯಸ್ಥಿತವಸಾನಂ ನಿಖಿಲ ಸೃಜನವೈರಕು ಪೂಜಕು ನರಕಕ್ಕೆಂ || ಪ್ರಿಯದಿಂದಿಂ ದೇವನೊಯ್ಯ ಕಾವ್ಯಪರಿಗಣಾಯಂ ಮಹಾ ಶ್ರೀಯಮಕ್ಕ [ಕ್ಕ] ಮಿದಂಕಾಯದೆ ಕೊ99 ಪಾಪಿಗೆ ಕುರುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದೊಳ್ಪಾರೋಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಣಿಕೊಳ್ಕೇಟಿ ಮಣಿವಂರಂ ಕಪಿಲಂವೇವಾಧ್ಯರಂ ಕೊಂದುದೊಣೆಯದು ಸಾಗುಮದಿನು ಸಾದಾಪುದಿಂ ಕ್ಷೀಲಾಕ್ಷರಂಧಾತ್ರಿಯೊಳು100 ಶಾಸನಮನುಸಿವಾ ನೇನದಿಂ ಲೇಖಿಸಿದ ರಿಕ್ಷ್ಯಗಂ ಮಹೀಮಂಡಿತಂ ಭಾಸುರಮತಿಬಣ್ಣಿ ಸಿದಂ ಪ್ರಿಃ ಸಣ್ಣನಾತಿಕಳನೇದು ಫೊಸಗನಂದದಿಂ || ಧರೆಯ ರೂಪಾರಿಚಕ್ರವರ್ತಿ ಚಂಡೋಜ ನಮಂ ಸಾತೋಣಜ ಕಂದರಂ ಮಂಗಳ ಮಹಾಶ್ರೀ ಶ್ರೀ

cells.remarks: Slab standing to the left inside the Agastyēśvara temple. This inscription belongs to the reign of Kalachurya Tribhuvanamalla-deva (Bijjaṇa) and introduces the one thousand (Mahājanas) of Pūli (modern Huli) the crest jewel of the Agrahāras, as erudite Vedic and Purāṇic scholars and philosophers. Among these, a body of hundred belonged to Śivayagēri, a suburb of Hūli. One of them was Perggaḍe Dāsirāja whose pedigree is given for five generations before him as follows:- Āditya of the Bhāradvāja gōtra, his son Dēvapayya, his son Perggaḍe Sōma, his son Mailapayya, his son Kālidāsa (married Rēviyakka) to whom was born Dāsirāja. Dāsirāja had three sons, viz. Mahādēva, Mālapayya and Kālidāsa. This perggaḍe Dāsirāja is stated to have endowed on the date specified in ll. 37-38, six mattar of land after purchasing it from the one thousand Mahājanas of Pūli headed by the Uroḍeya, for the renovation and repairs of the well called Nāgavāvi which is comparable to Vāraṇāsi, for the maintenance of a charity piotta and for the keeping of hearths (sacrificial fires?). The inscription further records another gift of two mattar of land made by the merchants and Bhaktas after purchasing it from the one thousand Mahājanas for eight-fold worship to the god Agastyēśvara in the same place. The details of date are:- Śaka 1084, Chitrabhanu, Pushya, ba. 2, Monday, Uttarayana-Sankranti, Vyatipata (= Monday, December 24, A. D. 1162, f. d. t. .55). [ḍ] dēśyākaṇḷē mahādēva budham || aśava tamya śīśyavāśyakam30 guṇam maḷāḷapanyunē mētyadāru || aśyāśyāṇadē śīyāṇam bhavanyasya31 va dā[r*]śīṇāśyāśyēśyāśīrēdīyā || jaśīnāśēṇīśēśyāṇavēdīyāśyē kuḷāśōyā32 ಗೃತ್ಥೆಯುಂ ಬವದೊಲಾಣನೆಯ್ದಾತನ ಭುಜಂಗಳನೆಲ್ಲವು ವ ಲ್ಲಭರಾದಿಯೆಂದೆ ಕಡಮಂದಮಂ ತಳವಂ ಸಲೆ ಬಿಜ್ಜಣದೇವ ಭೂಪು-33 ಣಂ [|*] ಪಲವಂಗಳುಂ ಸೂಲದ ಮಿನದೊರೆದೊಲ್ಲ ಕರುಳ್ಳಳು ಜೋಲ್ಲರಿಂಕಳಂ ಸುಲಿದು ಕಿತ್ತನ ಹುತ್ತಿ ರೇಣದವಟ್ಟಿಯಂ ಚಮನೆ34 [|*] ಪಾಮವ ಭಟ್ಟಕ್ಕಳ ಪಣ್ಣಲೆಯಿಂ ನೋಡಲಾ ಸುರುಮ[ಕು]ಗುಣ್ಣ್ಯವಾಯ್ತುಜಾದು ಗೆಲ್ಲೆ ಬಜ್ಜಣದೇವಭೂಪನ || ಸ್ಯಸ ಸನಸ್ಯ ಭವನಾ-35 ಶ್ರಯಂ ಶ್ರೀ ಸ್ಯಕೃತ್ಥವಭ ಮಹಾರಾಜರಾಜ ರಾಜೇಶ್ವರಂ ಕಳಾಣಪುರದರಾಘಿತ್ತರಂ ಡಮರುಂತಾಕಯ್ಯಂ ನಿರ್ಗತಾಸನಂ ಪರಾಕ್ರಮ [|*]36 ಣಂ ಶ್ರೀಮತ್ಕಳಚುಂಯ್ಯ ಭುಜಬಳ ಚಕ್ರವರ್ತಿ ಶ್ರೀಭುಜವನಲ್ಲದೇವವಜೇರಾಯಮುತ್ತ ರೇಣ್ತರಾಪದ್ಯದ ಪ್ರಭದವನಾನಾ-37 ಕ್ಕತಾರಂ ಸಲುತಮರೆ || ಶ್ರೀ ಮಜ್ಜಕವಳಂ ಗಂಳ ನೇಯ ಚಿತ್ರಭಾನುಸಂವತ್ಸರದ ಪುಷ್ಯ ಬಹುಳ ೩ ಸೋಮವಾರದಂದುತ್ತರಾಯಣ ಸಂಕ್ರಾ[ಂತಿ]-38 ಯಲು ನೃತಿಹಪಾತಂ ಕಳಂದಿ ದಿವ್ಯ ತಿಥಿಯಲು ಧರ್ಮಕಾವ್ಯನಿಮಿತ್ತಂ ಪೆಗ್ಗಡೆದಾಸರಾಜಂ ಶ್ರೀನನ್ನಹಾಗುಹಾರಂ ಪೂರಿಯ [ಊರ] ದೇ-39 ದೆಯ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಸಾಸಿವ್ಯಮಹಾಜನಂಗಳ ದಿವ್ಯ ಶೀಪಾದಪದ್ಮಂಗಳಂ ದೃನ್ನಪೂರ್ವಕಮಾರಾಧಿಪ ನಾರಾಯಣಶಿಯ ಸಮಾನವನ್ನ ನಾಗರವಾಲೀಯ ಖಂಡ-40 ಸ್ಪುಟಿತಜೀರ್ಣೋದ್ಧಾರಕ್ಕಮ್ಮಲ್ಲಿಯ ಧರ್ಮೋತ್ಸಾಹ ಮಗ್ಗಿತ್ತಗೊರಯ್ಯಗನಿಂದಕೊಳ್ಳಗೇರಿಯ ಹಾಲ ಹೆಸಮಗೊರಗೆ ಸವ್ಯ ನಮ-41 ಕ್ಕಮಾಗಿ ಬಿಟ್ಟು ಸುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದ ೫ ಸೀಮೆ ಮೋದಲು ತಕ್ಕಯ ಶಕ | ತೆಂಕಣ ಸೀಮೆನಾಗರ ಮಿಂದಿಯ ಕೇಶವದೇವ ಭೂಮಿ ಪಡುವಣ ಸೀ-42 ಮೆ | ಪೆಗ್ಗಡೆ ಶಕದಯ್ಯನಾಯಕನ ಸವ್ಯ ಭೂಮಿ ಬಡಗಣ ಸೀಮೆ | ಯೋರಂದಗೆರಿಗೆಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯಾಗಿ ಕೊಳ್ಳೆ ಭೂಮಿ | ಇತ್ಯೇ ದಿವ್ಯ [ಮ]-43 ನಾವ್ಯಾಯಮುವಾಡೊಡಂ ಸವ್ಯನಮಸ್ಕಮಾಗಿ ಸವ್ಯಮ್ಯಾದಂ ಸವ್ಯಮ್ಯಾದಿಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾಲಿಸು || ಮಂಗಳಮಹಾ ಶ್ರೀ ಶ್ರೀ44 ಱ ಆ ಪುಣ್ಯತಿಥಿಯೊಲ್ಲಿಯ ಪಟ್ಟಮಾದರಾದ ಶ್ರೀಮದಗ್ನೀಶ್ವರ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನಧಾಜ್ಞಾನ ನಿಮಿತ್ತಂ ಕೊಳ್ಳಗೇರಿಯ ಹಾಲ-45 ಹಸುಗೆಯೊಗೆ ಸವ್ಯಮಸ್ಕಮಾಗಿ ಯೂರೆದಿದೆಯ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಸಾಸಿವ್ಯಮಹಾಜನಂಗಳಂದರಿಯೊಡೇದೆಯ46 ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಭಕ್ತ್ಯಜನಂಗಳಾರಾಧಿಸಿ ಪಡದು ಬಿಟ್ಟ ಮತ್ರರದದಜ ಸೀಮೆ ಮೋದಲುಮೇಲೇಶ್ವರ ದೇವರ ಭೂಮಿ47 ತೆಂಕಲು ಜನನೇಜಿಯ ದಾರಿ ಪಡುವಲು ಕರಭಣು ಬಡಗಲು ಮೇಳೇಶ್ವರದೇವಭೂಮಿ | ಇನಿತಂ ನಿಶ್ಚಯಮಾ-48 ಗಿ ಭಾವಿಸುವುದಿ ಧಮ್ಮಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಪಾಲೈಶ್ವರ್ಯನಮೋಹಂ ಸಕುಳಂ ನಿಗೋದಕಳದೇವಭೂಳಂ || ಮಹಾಪಾಠಕಂ ಮನನೊಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂದವನ್ನೆ ರಕ್ಷಿಸು-49 ವಡೇಮಂಗಳಮಾಯುಷ್ಯವೃದ್ಧನಮಹಾಲಕ್ಷ್ಮೀ ನಿಮ್ಮಳ ಯಶಂ ಭದ್ರಂ ಶುಭಂಮಂಗಳಂ || ಸ್ವದತ್ತಂ ಪರದತ್ತಂ ವಾಯೋ ಹರೇತಿ ವಸುಂ-50 [ಭ] ದಾಂ ಪಷಿಂ ಮಹಾಸಹಸ್ರಾಣಿ ನಿಶ್ಚಯಾಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ಕ್ಷಮಿ ||

cells.remarks: received through Mr. N. S. Kamalapur, B.A., LL.B., Dharwar. The subjoined copper-plate grant is engraved on a set of three plates of which the first and the last plate bear writing on one side only. The plates measure 10 1/4" X 6 1/4" X 1/4" each and are joined to a circular ring by a hole cut into the centre of the left margin. A rectangular seal (1 7/8" X 1 1/2") bearing the representation of a standing tiger facing east with the sun and moon above is fastened to the ring. The plates without the seal weigh 270 tolas. The seal weighs 12 1/4 tolas. The inscription is written in the Nagari alphabet which furnishes one of the earliest specimens of the Nandi-Nagari that subsequently became the ruling alphabet of the Vijayanagara period. The language is Sanskrit. The inscription opens with an invocation to Vishnu to protect the Earth and after two verses in praise of the ruling king and the moon, proceeds to the genealogy of king Viraballala as follows:- In the lunar race which produced the Lord of Lakshmi (i. e. Krishna) was born one known by the name of Gajasatva (l. 10) who killed a tiger by a blue shaft (nila-salakaya) at the injunction of a sage by the words hoyi sala (pierce, oh, Sala) in Kannada. Thereafter Hoysala became the name of his family. His son was Vinayaditya to whom was born Erreyanga-mahipala, who was Vishnu and the latter's son was Narasimha. Narasimha's son was Vira-Ballala. King Viraballala is stated to have granted on the date specified in ll. 40-43, the two villages Huggilur and Honnur included in Soge-Twelve. 58 No. 28. Copper-plate grant of Hoysala Vira-Ballala II. Saka 1126. First plate II side R. S. Panchamukhi. of the district of Koḷali-Five hundred, to the Mahajana (used collectively for the Mahajanas) of the mahāgrahāra village Pushpapatalika. At the time of the gift, the king had sojourned at Siligoda with his army. Among the boundaries specified in ll. 49 to 84, the following places are mentioned. (I) In regard to Huggilūr :- Sōge, Bāguli, Mosalagaḍa, Basurikōḍa, Haḍagile, Muḍunira. (II) In regard to Honnūr :- Ānevaḷḷa (stream), Kurruviti, Kurruvaḍa. The grant of Huggilūr amounted to shaṭsahasra (6000) together with the rights over water and rocks (jala-pāshāṇa) in them. Shatsahasra (Six Thousand) represented, presumably, the yielding capacity or the revenue income of the village. The details of date are :- Saka 1126 (in words), Raktākshi, Āsvayuja, lunar eclipse. They regularly correspond to Sunday, October 10, A. D. 1204. This was a day of lunar eclipse. This is the first and the only copperplate charter known so far that belongs to the Hoysaḷa king Vīraballāḷa II. Pushpapatalika is Hūvina-Haḍagali, in the Harapanahalli Taluk of the Bellary district. I plate; II side 59 II plate, I side No. 28. (Cont.) Second plate, I side 60 R. S. Panchamukhi. II plate; II side 61 III plate | I side 62 Plate IV-c. No. 28. (Cont.) Second plate, II side R. S. Panchamukhi.

text.remarks:
received through Mr. N. S. Kamalapur, B.A., LL.B., Dharwar.
The subjoined copper-plate grant is engraved on a set of three plates of which the first and the last plate bear writing on one side only. The plates measure 10 1/4" X 6 1/4" X 1/4" each and are joined to a circular ring by a hole cut into the centre of the left margin. A rectangular seal (1 7/8" X 1 1/2") bearing the representation of a standing tiger facing east with the sun and moon above is fastened to the ring. The plates without the seal weigh 270 tolas. The seal weighs 12 1/4 tolas.
The inscription is written in the Nagari alphabet which furnishes one of the earliest specimens of the Nandi-Nagari that subsequently became the ruling alphabet of the Vijayanagara period. The language is Sanskrit.
The inscription opens with an invocation to Vishnu to protect the Earth and after two verses in praise of the ruling king and the moon, proceeds to the genealogy of king Viraballala as follows:- In the lunar race which produced the Lord of Lakshmi (i. e. Krishna) was born one known by the name of Gajasatva (l. 10) who killed a tiger by a blue shaft (nila-salakaya) at the injunction of a sage by the words hoyi sala (pierce, oh, Sala) in Kannada. Thereafter Hoysala became the name of his family. His son was Vinayaditya to whom was born Erreyanga-mahipala, who was Vishnu and the latter's son was Narasimha. Narasimha's son was Vira-Ballala.
King Viraballala is stated to have granted on the date specified in ll. 40-43, the two villages Huggilur and Honnur included in Soge-Twelve.
58

of the district of Koḷali-Five hundred, to the Mahajana (used collectively for the Mahajanas) of the mahāgrahāra village Pushpapatalika. At the time of the gift, the king had sojourned at Siligoda with his army.
Among the boundaries specified in ll. 49 to 84, the following places are mentioned. (I) In regard to Huggilūr :- Sōge, Bāguli, Mosalagaḍa, Basurikōḍa, Haḍagile, Muḍunira. (II) In regard to Honnūr :- Ānevaḷḷa (stream), Kurruviti, Kurruvaḍa.
The grant of Huggilūr amounted to shaṭsahasra (6000) together with the rights over water and rocks (jala-pāshāṇa) in them. Shatsahasra (Six Thousand) represented, presumably, the yielding capacity or the revenue income of the village.
The details of date are :- Saka 1126 (in words), Raktākshi, Āsvayuja, lunar eclipse. They regularly correspond to Sunday, October 10, A. D. 1204. This was a day of lunar eclipse.
This is the first and the only copperplate charter known so far that belongs to the Hoysaḷa king Vīraballāḷa II.
Pushpapatalika is Hūvina-Haḍagali, in the Harapanahalli Taluk of the Bellary district.

cells.remarks: On a pillar in the Chidambarēśvara temple. The inscription is badly damaged and mutilated on the left side. From what is preserved of it, it purports to belong to the Hoysaḷa king Vīra Ballāḷa II (?) and seems to record a gift of house-sites and oil-mill made to Gaṅga-Kandarpa Brahmajina[laya]. In lines 6 to 24, a 63 certain . . . Kirtipaṇḍita-Chikkayyaṅgalu evidently of the Ganga- Kandarpa Brahmajinalaya, Harihara son of Narana-Bhaṭṭa and some Seṭṭis are mentioned among the donors of a gift made for the benefit of a god and probably entrusted to the mahājanas of the place. Permadiya-basadi is mentioned. Of the date, only Vaiśākha, śu. 7, is preserved. Paleography of the record and the reference to the Hoysaṇa-Chakravartin point to the age of the inscription as 12th to 13th century A.D. Plate IV-d. No. 28. (Cont.) Third plate, I side Seal. R. S. Panchamukhi. 65

cells.remarks: Slab set up in the Panchalingesvara temple. This inscription belongs to the reign of Yadanarayana Pratapachakravarti Singhanadeva who ruling the kingdom from the nelevidu at Devagiri. It records the foundation of a Saiva settlement, Sivapura by Jogadeva-chamupa, younger brother of Purushottama-Dandanayaka at the command of the king and registers grants of land made by him to the Brahmans at the following four villages viz. Munipura (i. e. Munavalli), Sindavage, Aganuru and Nagarapura. Munipura also called Munavalli was situated in Toragale-nadu (a sub-division) of Kuntala. Jogadeva is stated to have granted the village Kallavole for repairs and renovations and for the daily worship in the temple of Svayambhu-Panchalingadeva on the date specified in lines 24 and 25. Several minor gifts are also recorded for the Brahmans of the Brahmapuri. The details of the date are: Saka 1145, Chitrabhanu, Kartika, su. Punnme, Monday, lunar eclipse and Vyatipata. They are irregular. The intended English equivalent for Chitrabhanu corresponding to Saka 1144 was Friday, October 21, A. D. 1222, on which day there was a lunar eclipse. In Saka 1146 which was Tarana, the given tithi fell on Monday, October 28, A. D. 1224; but it was not a day of lunar eclipse. The former is the date evidently intended by the record. 66 67 [Footnote 1] The letter ಱ is written above the line.

ನಾಲ್ಕು ದಿಕಾರದ ಮದಧಿಕಾರಿಯ [ಕ]

ಪಟ್ಟಿಯಣಗಳೊ ಯೆಲುನಡೆ ಹಂ

ಸುಮವ || ಸ್ವದತ್ತ ಪರದತ್ತ
67 ಯೋ ಹರೇತಿ ವಸುಂಧರಾ ಷಷ್ಟಿವರ್ಷ ಸಹಸ್ರಾಣಿ ವಿನ್ಯಾಯಾ ಜಾಯತೇ ಕ್ರಿಮಿ ||

text.remarks:
Slab set up in the Panchalingesvara temple.
This inscription belongs to the reign of Yadanarayana Pratapachakravarti Singhanadeva who ruling the kingdom from the nelevidu at Devagiri. It records the foundation of a Saiva settlement, Sivapura by Jogadeva-chamupa, younger brother of Purushottama-Dandanayaka at the command of the king and registers grants of land made by him to the Brahmans at the following four villages viz. Munipura (i. e. Munavalli), Sindavage, Aganuru and Nagarapura. Munipura also called Munavalli was situated in Toragale-nadu (a sub-division) of Kuntala. Jogadeva is stated to have granted the village Kallavole for repairs and renovations and for the daily worship in the temple of Svayambhu-Panchalingadeva on the date specified in lines 24 and 25. Several minor gifts are also recorded for the Brahmans of the Brahmapuri.
The details of the date are: Saka 1145, Chitrabhanu, Kartika, su. Punnme, Monday, lunar eclipse and Vyatipata. They are irregular. The intended English equivalent for Chitrabhanu corresponding to Saka 1144 was Friday, October 21, A. D. 1222, on which day there was a lunar eclipse. In Saka 1146 which was Tarana, the given tithi fell on Monday, October 28, A. D. 1224; but it was not a day of lunar eclipse. The former is the date evidently intended by the record.
66
67

ಸಂಸೋಭ್ಯಮೆಂದೊಪ್ಪುತ್ತಿಪ್ಪ ಶ್ರೀ ಚೌಡಬ್ಯಕೃತಕೃತ್ಯನಾದಗುನಿ7 ವಜಕೃತ್ಯ ಕರದ್ವಾಜದತ್ರಿ ಶ್ರೀ ವಿಶ್ವಮಿತ್ರರಿಂದಂ ಮುನಿಪುರಮೆಸಗೊಂ ಕೇಟಿಶಭಂಗ-8 ಳಂದೊ || ಪಮುತ್ತುರೋಪನವನಮಂತೊದೊಡೆ || ತೆಂಗು ಕಂತುಗು ಜಂಬುವದ ಮಾಧವಳಂಪನಸಾಬ-9 ಣಿಸಿನಾಗರಂಗಳನಗಣಿತಶುಭರೊಹಂನಿಸುಪಾಟಿಶಪಾಜಕತ ಪುಂಡಗನವಣೋತ್ ಕತ್ತಲಿಸುತಪ್ಪಿ ಲೇವ್ಯಗಳಂ ಮ-10 ದಾಲಯುಂ ಶ್ರೀಗಿದು ಜನ್ಮಭೂಮಿಯೆನಿಸುಕುಂ ಮುನಿವಳ್ಳ ಸದಾಶಕಾಲಮುಂ || ಸನಕಸನಂದನಾದಿ ಜಮದಗ್ನಿಬಾಧಾಕೃತ್ಯ-11 ತಾಣನಿ ಮುನಿಪುರನಿಂತಿದಂ ಮುದದೆ ರಕ್ಷಿಸುತಪ್ಪನು ಪಂಚಲಿಂಗೇನಲುದನಿದನತತು ಪುರೋಪ-12 ವನ ಸಾಸ್ರ್ವ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಿಯೊಳುನವನಿತೆಯುಂ ಧನಕನಕಂಗಳದೇವಸೇನಂ ಧರೆ ಮೇರುಶಾಸನಕರುಳ್ಯನಂ || ಸ್ಯ್ಕೀ(೨) ಶ್ರೀ ಸಿದ್ದಿಂನಲಂ13 ಮಹಾರಾಜಾಧಿರಾಜ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ ಪರಮಭಟ್ಟಾರಕಂ ಶ್ರೀಮತು ಜೈತುಗಿದೇವಕುಳ-14 ಕಮಳಮಾರ್ತಂಡನಾದ ಯಾದವನಾರಾಯಣ15 ಌ ಪ್ರತಾಪಚಕ್ರವರ್ತಿ ಶ್ರೀಮತು ಸಿಂಘಣದೇವರೆರಡರ ದೇವನಗಿರಿಯ ನೆಲೆವೀದಿನೋಳು ಸುಖಸಂಕಥಾವಿನೋದದಿಂ ರಾಜ್ಯಂಗಯ್ಯು-16 ತ್ತಮಿರ್ದರಿರ್ದು || ಯಾದವರಾಯನ ಸಿರೀಭುಜಮಹಿಮಿತ ತನ ಭುಜಾಧಿರಾದರೆಯೊಳು ಸಾದಿಸಿವೈರಿಭೂಪಜಯ ದೆಸೆಯನಕ್ಕಳಿಗಂ-17 ಡು ರೇಣಿಯೊಂ ಮೇದಿನಿಯೊಳೆಲ್ಲತ್ರ ತಗ್ಗಾಗಿ ಮಹೋನ್ನತವಿತತ ರಾಜ್ಯದಿಂ ಬಾದಿಗುದಂಡದಂಡಿತ ಸಕಳರಾಜಮಂಡಳಂ ||18 ಯಾದವಾಧಿರಾಜ್ಯಂ ಧಾತ್ರಿಯಂ ಲೇಲಿರಯನಲ್ಕು ಸಿಂಘಣೇಂದ್ರನ ಸುರೇಂದ್ರನವೊಲು ನಿಜಕುಲಂ || ಜಗತಹಗುಂಡಿಗದೊಪ್ಪಿಜಂ ಜಗಮನ್ಯಾ-19 ದೇವಂದೆ ಪಾಲಪುದೆಂದಿ ಜಗದೀಶಕಮನಿತ್ತಂ ಜಗದಳ ಪುರುಷೋತ್ತಮಂಗೆ ಸಿಂಘಣ20 ರಾಯನು || ಧರ್ಮ್ಮಪ್ರಸಂಗದಿಂದೆ ನೆಮ್ಮೆಗೆ ಮೇರು ಸು-20 ಭಣೋತ್ಸವಂ ಶಿವಪುರಂ ನಿಮ್ಮಿಪುದೆಂದೆ ಪುರುಷೋತ್ತಮ ಧರ್ಮ್ಮದ್ಯೋಗಮನನೆ21 ಜೋಗಳದೇವಂಗೆ || ಸ್ವಿಕಾರಮನೆ ಪುಣ್ಯತಿಥಿ ವರಶಿಕಾಫೀಗೆ ಮೇರು ತಾರಾ-21 ಜಳದಿ ಪುರುಷನಿಧಿ ಪುರುಷೋತ್ತಮ ಪುರುಷೋತ್ತಮನುದಕ ದಕ್ಕೆ ಮೇಲವಾಗುತ್ತಂ ||22 ಮತ್ಸಮ ಜೋಗಳದೇವನ ವಂಶಾವಳಾರವದೊಡನೆ ||22 ೧ ಗಿರಿಜೇಶ ಪಂಚಲಿಂಗಂ ವದದ ಜಿಜಳಸಮನ್ವಿತಂ ವಾಸಿತ್ಯ ಮೈತ್ರವದರಂ ಕವುಂದಿಂತ್ಯ23 ಗೋತ್ತಂ ಜಡಕಳಣಿಕಾಳಕಳಂಕ ರಾಮದೇವಂ23 ಸಿರ ಸತ್ಯಂ ಮಾನಿಲೋಕಾಂಬಿಕೆ ಜನನಿ ಲಕ್ಶ್ಮಿಯರಿಗು ಗೋಭ್ಯಾಯು ಲಕ್ಶ್ಮೀವರಪುತ್ರಂ24 ಸೋಮನಾಥಂ ಶಿವದೇವನೊಳೆ ಧರ್ಮ್ಮಯೋ ಜೋಗೇ-24 ದೇವಂ || ಮತ್ಸಮ ಜೋಗಳದೇವ ಪಲವು ದೇಶಾಧಿಕಾರಮಂ ಮಾಡಿ ಸುಖದಿಂದಲ್ಲಿ25 ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ ಶ್ರೀಮತು ಸಕವರ್ಷ ೧೧೯೩ನೆಯ ಚಿತ್ರ-25 ಭಾನು ಸಂವತ್ಸರದ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕ ಶುದ್ಧ ಪುಣ್ಣಮಿ ಸೋಮವಾರ ಸೋಮಗ್ರಹಣ26 ಬೃಹಸ್ಪತಾದಿತ್ಯ || ಸ್ವಯಂಭು ಶ್ರೀಪಂಚಲಿಂಗದೇವರಿಗೆ ಮಾಟಿ-26 ಕೂಟ ಪ್ರಸಾದಕ್ಕೂಂ ಖಂಡಸ್ಪುಟಿತ ಜಿರ್ಣೋದ್ಧಾರ ನಿತ್ಯನೈವೇದ್ಯಮಭೋಗ ರಂಗ27 ಭೋಗ ಭಕ್ತಕ್ಕೂ ಶ್ರೀಮತು ಸಿಂಘಣದೇವ-27 ಸತ್ಯಾಧಿಕಾರಿ ಪುರುಷೋತ್ತಮ ಧರ್ಮ್ಮಾಧಿಕಾರ ನಿಯಾಮಮಂ ಜೋಗಳದೇವ ಸಬ್ಬ28 ನಮ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಕಲ್ಪಸೊಳುಂ ಸಕಲಂ-28 ಣ್ಯ ಧಾರಾಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ಮಾಡಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟ || ವರಲಕ್ಶ್ಮೀಪತಿ ಜೋಗಳದೇವನೊಳೆ ಶ್ರೀ ಪಂಚ29 ಲಿಂಗಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಸ್ಥಿರದಿ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಕಳ್ಯಾಣಕಂ29 ಸಂಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂತ್ತನಸಾದದಿಂ ಚೈತ್ರ ಪವಿತ್ರಕಂ ಸ್ಯಟಿತಕಣ್ಯಗಾದ್ಯರ ಶಕ್ತಿದಂ30 ಧರಣೀಶರು ಪ್ರಜಾವರ್ಗಪಾಲಕ ಚಂ-30 ದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯರುಳ್ಳನೊ || ಪುರುಷೋತ್ತಮಸಮಾನುಜ ಶಕಪುತ್ರಂ ಶ್ರೀ ಜೋಗಳದೇವ ದಂಡಾ31 ಧೀಶಂ ಸ್ಥಿರದಮನೆ ಶಿವಪುರಂ ಧರಿಮೇ-31 ರು ಶಕಕಾಲವಳನಂ ದ್ವಿಜಗ್ರಾತ್ಸಂ || ಪ್ರಿತಿ ಹದಿನಾಜ ಶಿವಪುರತ್ತಮವಿಪ್ರರಿಗೆ32 ಜೋಗಳದೇವ ಜಮೂನಪಂ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಕಮ್ಮನಿಂದುಂ32 ಹೆಪ್ಪುವರದುನಬಂ ನಾರಕದೊಳೆ || ಮತ್ಸಮದಾನವಾಪುರೊದೊಡನೆ || ದಂಡಾಧೀಶಂ || ಮತ್ಸ-35 ವತ್ಸಪ್ರಸ್ತವನೊಳು || ಕ್ಯಾಗದ ಪೆಂಟಿನ ನೆಲ ಮನಿಪುರದ ಮನಿಪುರದ ತೋಟಿನೊಳ್36 ಸರ್ವ(1)ಫಲದ ಭೋಗ್ಯದ ನನಯ ಬಲುದ್ಯೋಗದ ಕಳತನದ ಬಲುಸಿನಾ-36 ಸ್ಥಿಂ ಕಮ್ಮಿಂ || ಧರಣೀಶನ ಪಂಚಲಿಂಗದಕಣ್ಯಗಾದ್ಯರಸದ ತೋಟಿನೊತ್ತ37 ವಹಣ್ಯಂತ ಸ್ತಿರಸತ್ಯಾಕ್ಯಾನ ಚಿತ್ರಮನಿಜಂ39 ಕುಗುರುಮನಾನ್ವಯಂ || ಲೋಕಶುಭ್ರರು || ಕರಣದಂಗಜರಾಮರತ್ನದೇವಂಗೆನಿಜ್ಞಾ40 ಸನ್ನಿಧಿ ತಾಂ ದೇವಕೀಂ-40 ಧಿಕ್ಕವನಲ್ಲೆ ಕಾವಬಲ್ಯೊದಾದ್ಯಾದಿಂ ಸತ್ಯದೊಡಲಿದಂ ಸಾಹಸದೊಲ್ಲಿಯಂ ಸಕಳ41 ಧರ್ಮ್ಮದ್ಯೋಗದಿನಾಜ ನಾಲರ ವುದೊಂದೆ ಮಾರುಲು ತಗ್ಗಿ ಹೋದ ಹೆಪ್ಪಟ್ಟಿ ತೇಶಲು ಹಳ್ಳ ಪಡುವಲಕ್ಕಸಾಲಿಗೆಯ44 ಬಡಗಲು ಹೆಬ್ಬಳ್ಳ ಹರಕಳಿಯ ಮುತ್ತೆ ದೆಂ-44 ದಕ್ಕಿ ಸೀಮೆ ಮಂಡಲ ಕಾಲದಾದೆನಿ ತೇಶಲು ಹಡತೇಗೆ ಪಡುವಲು ಕಜುವನೆಟ್ಟ45 ಬಡಗಲು ಹವಿನಕಳ್ಳ ಹೆಬ್ಬಟ್ಟಿ ದೇವ-45 ಣಂ ತೇಶಲು ಯುಗಾದಿತ್ಯದಿಂ ಪಡುವಲು ಶ್ರೀರಾಮಗಂಗೆಯಂ ಬಡಗಲು ನಟ್ಟ ಕಳ್ಳಂ46 ಮಂಡಲು ಯೆಡೆದೊಣಟಿ ಕುರುಯನಸೀ-46 ಕ್ಕಂ ಸಿದ್ಧಿಯ ಹರಿಕೆಳಕಳು ಸಂಕಲಬಾಯ ಅಕ್ಕಿಳೆ ಬಚ್ಚಿ ಸುಂಕ ಸಭ್ಯತಾಭ47 ಪರಿಹಾವ ಯಾದೊಣ್ಣೆಕ್ಕಿ || ಯೆಲೆಯ ಹೆಜಿಗೆಂ ವಿಸ-47 ಪ್ಪೊದು ಸ್ವಗತ ಸಂಘನತ್ತಿ ಸೋಮವಾರದಲು ನಿವಾಳಗೆ ಗಾಣಕ್ಕೆ ಯೊಂಕ್ಕಿ ಸೋಸನಿಗೆ48 ಯೆರಡು ದೇವಂಗೆ ನಸೇವ ಗಾಣವೊಂ-1 The letter ಱ is written above the line.48 ದುಯುಜನಾತಿಕೊಲ್ಲಲು ಕೊಟ್ಟ ತಾಜಾನ ಕಂದಗಿಯಲೆ ಕೊಯಲಾಲಾ ಕೊಯಲು ಕುಡುವರುಯೆಲೆಯು ತೋಟಗೇದ[ದೊ]49 ದನರು ಯರಸಾದಿಕಾರಗಳು ಸುಂಕವಂ ಮನಿಪುವರು ಪುರೋಳಿಗರು ತಂಬುಲಿಗರುಹುಟ್ಟಿದ ಧಾನ್ಯದೊಳು ದೀಕ್ಷ್ಯಮಾಡಿ ಕು[ಡ]-50 ವರು ಹೊದೊದೊಡನೆ ಮಡಿಲೊ ತೋಟದ ಸೀಮೆ ಶ್ರೀ ರಾಮವಗೆ ಪಡುವಣ ಸೀಮೆಬದಿಯತೋಟ ಬಗಣ ಸೀಮೆ51 ಯೆಲೆತೋಟದ ಮುತ್ತಂ ತೋಟದೊಟದ ಯೆಲೆಯುಳ್ಳಯಯುತ್ತರಕ್ಕೂ ಸೀಮೆಮೂಡಲು ಶ್ರೀರಾಮವಗೆ ತೆಂಕಣ ಪಡುವ-52 ಬಡಗಣ ಸೀಮೆ ನಷ್ಟಕಳ್ಳು ಸುರುಗನ ಹಾಲಲು ಹೊದೊದೊಟ ಮಂಜು ಶ್ರೀ ಮಾಧವನಾರಾಯಣನಿಗೆ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾಲ ಮಾಡಿ53 ಆ ದೇವರಿ ಆಂಗಭೋಗ ರಂಗಭೋಗಕ್ಕೆ ಸರ್ವನಮಸ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಸತ್ರಿಯಸಹಿತಯಂಸಟಬಂಧ ದಾರಾಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ಮಾಡಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಮುವ[ತ್ತಿ]54 ಯಂ ಮಂಡಲವು ಹೆಗ್ಗಡಿ ತೋಟಲು ಶ್ರೀ ರಾಮಗಂಗೊಯಲು ಪಡುವಲು ನಷ್ಟಕಳ್ಳುಬಡಗಲು ಯೆಲೆತೋಟದ ಕುಳವಾಯನಲು-55 ಮುತ್ತಮಪ್ಪಸುವದೊಳು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪುರಿಯ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರಿಗೆ ಧಾರಾಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಟ್ಟ ಪ್ರೀತಿ ಕಡಕುಳದೊರದು ಬಳ್ಳಿಗೇರಿಯಲೆರಡು ಕುಳುಕುಂದದಲೆರ56 ಕ್ಕೈಸಿಲುಲೆರಡು ಕುರುಳನೂಲದೊಳು ಬಂಸಿಪುರಲೆರಡು ದಾಡಿಯ ಬಾವಿಯಲೆರಡುಗೋವಿನನಲೆರಡು ಜಣಿಗಾಧನವನನೂಲರಡು ಹಳೆ [ವ]57 ಲ್ಲೊ ಆ ಮತ್ತಂ ತೋಟದೊನೆಯಕರು ಮುನಿದ್ರಾವಲ್ಲಿಯ ಸವಸುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲಿ ಶಿವಪುರಕಂನಂ [ದೊ] ಶಾಸನಕಂ ಅರುಮತ್ತೊಕ್ಕಲುಗಳ ಮದನನಪ್ಪಕರಿಯನಾ-58 ಜ್ಞಾಪ್ಯಾಗಿ ಸಜೊಲಣ್ಯಂ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಧಾರಾಪೂರ್ವಕವಾಗಿ ಹದಮುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲಿ ಭೂಮಿಯಹೀಮಪದ್ಧತಿಯಿಂದೊಡನೆ ಈಶಾನದತ್ತ ತೋಟದ59 ದೆಸೆ || ಕಂ || ತೋಟದಾವೃತ್ತಿಸೆಯು ತೋಟಕ್ಕಾರಂ ಜಿನೇಂದ್ರ ಭವನಮಿಸುತಂ ಮತ್ತಂಕಾರಣಕೆ ಮಸತ ಕಚ್ಚು ಗೋಶುರನೊ ತೆಂಗೆ [ಬ]60 ರಕ್ಕಂ ದೋಷ[ದಿ] ಆ ತೋಟದ ಮೆರೆಯಂ ಸವದನ ಮಾಡಿ [ಕ]ಣಿತರ ಕಾಲಸಿಟ್ಟಿಯತೋಟದ ವಾಯುವ್ಯದಿಂ ತೆಂಕಮುಂದಾಗಿ ದೇವದಮ್ಮ61 ರಗೆ [ರುಂಬ] ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಯ ನಾಲ್ವತ್ತೈಯನಬಿನವನ ತೋಟದಿಂ ಪಡುವನ ಮುಖಕಳ್ಳವಳಿಗೆ ಹೋದ ಬಟ್ಟಿ ಮಲ್ಲಹಾರಿ ರುಪಿತಧಾರಿ62 ದಗಲು ಕಜುಗುಶೆಯ ಮಧ್ಯದೊ ಕುನ್ನೆಯಂ ಕೆಳಗೆ ಮೊದಲರ ಬಟ್ಟಿಯಂ ಕೊಡಗದಕೇಲು ಕಾಲಕವೆಯಾಲಾ ಹೋದಕಳ್ಳ ಸುಂ63 ದಕ್ಷಿಣೆಯೊಂ ತೋಟದಾವೃತ್ತಿ || ಇತಿ ಸೀಮಾಕ್ರಮಂ ಈ ಮಳಗೆಯ ತೋಟದ ತೋಟಗಸಕಲ ಸಾಮ್ಮ್ಯವನ್ನೊಪ್ಪಿ [ಶ್ರೀ]64 ಜೇಲಿಂಗ ದೇವರದು ದಸದೊಯಸಕಲ್ಲಣವಧಮ್ಮ ಪ್ರಿಯ ಅಂಬಲ ಯೊ ಧಮ್ಮ್ಯಮಂನಾಲ್ಕು ದಿಕಾರದ ಮದಧಿಕಾರಿಯ [ಕ]65 ಸುಂಕಂ ಸಮಯ ಜಕ್ಕನವಕ ಅಯನವ್ಯಯಂ ಸಾಸನ್ಯನಂ ನಾಲ್ಕುಪಟ್ಟಿಯಣಗಳೊ ಯೆಲುನಡೆ ಹಂ66 ರಿಯ ಪ್ರಭೆಯ ನಾನಾದೇಸಿಗಳು ಭೂಮಿಜಲಧರಾಧ್ಯಾಕೃತಾರಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾಲಸುಮವ || ಸ್ವದತ್ತ ಪರದತ್ತ67 ಯೋ ಹರೇತಿ ವಸುಂಧರಾ ಷಷ್ಟಿವರ್ಷ ಸಹಸ್ರಾಣಿ ವಿನ್ಯಾಯಾ ಜಾಯತೇ ಕ್ರಿಮಿ ||

cells.remarks: Slab set up in front of the Udachavva temple in the fort. After invocation to Sambhu, the inscription describes in ll. 3-9 Munindravalli included in Toregale Six Thousand district and intro- duces king Kandhararaya 'born in the race of Vishnu', 'lord of Dvaravatipura,' son of Jaitugi and grandson of Sinhana as ruling the country from the nelevidu at Devagiri. On the date specified in ll. 20- 22, the sixty Vokkals of Munindravalli called Ratnagara i.e. mine of jewels, Ugura-Three Hundred, the Five Hundred and four, the Eight Hittus and the Five Mathasthala (body) and other proprietors (samya- vantaru) are stated to have made an endowment of four mattar of land and a garden with hundred and twenty-seven pits for areca plants and a flower garden, for conducting the festivals of chaitra and pavitra, burning perpetual lamps and maintaining worship and offerings in the temple of Jagadisvara. The gift was entrusted to the Kalamukha priest Rayarajaguru Sarvesvaradeva described as the promoter of the philo- sophy of Lakulagama, a moving incarnation of the Linga (jamgamalin- gavatararum), purifier of the two families (i.e. on the side of his father and mother) and well-versed in Rigveda, Samaveda, Atharva- (1) The letter is written above the line. vēda, Yajurvēda (Yajurvēda), Vēdānta, the six systems of Tarka, Vyākaraṇa, Chhandas (prosody), Nighaṇṭu (lexicon), Kāvya (poetry), Nāṭaka (drama) and other sciences. Sarvēśvara's son was Kriyāśakti whose son was Sōmēśvara. The line of the priests (gurupilige) given here had spiritual control over the following temples:- Mallēśvara of Veḷugrāma, Kalidēva of the piriyagrahāra Nēsarige, Ballēśvara of Gōkāge, Vijayamēśvara of Kottuṃbāgi of Halasige-Twelve Thousand and Kalidēva of Gōḷihalli. Bommarasa a favourite of Daṇḍanāyaka Basavadēva a devotee of Mahēśvara (Māhēśvara) composed the record. The inscription is important as a document showing the spread of the Lākula influence in Karnatak in the 13th century A. D. The details of date are :- Śaka 1174, Virōdhikṛit, Jyēshṭha, ba. amāvāsye, solar eclipse, Friday. In Virōdhikṛit (=Śaka 1173), the given tithi fell on Tuesday, June 8, A. D. 1251 on which day there was no solar eclipse. For Śaka 1174, the tithi Jyēshṭha, amāvāsye occurred on Friday, June 7, A. D. 1252; f. d. t. . 71, but no solar eclipse. The latter is probably the intended date of the record. (1) The letter is written below the line. samavada || śrīmatu rā- ttagaḷaṁ nāḷa- dēvaru- saṣṭinadalu kē- kaḍahē- pratibhaṁvina nēsaḷaru vijayavē- [ḷa] ḷyā-

text.remarks:
Slab set up in front of the Udachavva temple in the fort.
After invocation to Sambhu, the inscription describes in ll. 3-9
Munindravalli included in Toregale Six Thousand district and intro-
duces king Kandhararaya 'born in the race of Vishnu', 'lord of
Dvaravatipura,' son of Jaitugi and grandson of Sinhana as ruling the
country from the nelevidu at Devagiri. On the date specified in ll. 20-
22, the sixty Vokkals of Munindravalli called Ratnagara i.e. mine of
jewels, Ugura-Three Hundred, the Five Hundred and four, the Eight
Hittus and the Five Mathasthala (body) and other proprietors (samya-
vantaru) are stated to have made an endowment of four mattar of land
and a garden with hundred and twenty-seven pits for areca plants and
a flower garden, for conducting the festivals of chaitra and pavitra,
burning perpetual lamps and maintaining worship and offerings in the
temple of Jagadisvara. The gift was entrusted to the Kalamukha priest
Rayarajaguru Sarvesvaradeva described as the promoter of the philo-
sophy of Lakulagama, a moving incarnation of the Linga (jamgamalin-
gavatararum), purifier of the two families (i.e. on the side of his
father and mother) and well-versed in Rigveda, Samaveda, Atharva-
(1) The letter is written above the line.
vēda, Yajurvēda (Yajurvēda), Vēdānta, the six systems of Tarka,
Vyākaraṇa, Chhandas (prosody), Nighaṇṭu (lexicon), Kāvya (poetry),
Nāṭaka (drama) and other sciences. Sarvēśvara's son was Kriyāśakti
whose son was Sōmēśvara. The line of the priests (gurupilige) given
here had spiritual control over the following temples:- Mallēśvara of
Veḷugrāma, Kalidēva of the piriyagrahāra Nēsarige, Ballēśvara of
Gōkāge, Vijayamēśvara of Kottuṃbāgi of Halasige-Twelve Thousand
and Kalidēva of Gōḷihalli. Bommarasa a favourite of Daṇḍanāyaka
Basavadēva a devotee of Mahēśvara (Māhēśvara) composed the record.
The inscription is important as a document showing the spread of
the Lākula influence in Karnatak in the 13th century A. D.
The details of date are :- Śaka 1174, Virōdhikṛit, Jyēshṭha, ba.
amāvāsye, solar eclipse, Friday. In Virōdhikṛit (=Śaka 1173), the given
tithi fell on Tuesday, June 8, A. D. 1251 on which day there was
no solar eclipse. For Śaka 1174, the tithi Jyēshṭha, amāvāsye occurred
on Friday, June 7, A. D. 1252; f. d. t. . 71, but no solar eclipse. The
latter is probably the intended date of the record.

cells.remarks: Fragment of stone lying in the Nārāyaṇa temple.. This damaged and partially broken record seems to refer itself to the time of the Raṭṭa chief Kartavirya and extols the one hundred mahā- janas of Kartavirypura on the banks of the Malāpahariṇī. On the date specified in ll. 23-24 Chamūpati Nagadeva, son of Divākara - chamūpa and grandson of Padmanābha of the Kaundinyagotra is stated to have installed the image of Śrī Varada-Janārdanadeva at Kartaviryapura. The one hundred Mahājanas endowed land measuring 1000 kammas, flower garden and a house for worship and decoration to the deity. Similar gifts are recorded for the same temple by Dēhāri Mādhava- Bhaṭṭa, the Mahājanas and. Lakshmīdēvarasa, brother of Nāgarasa (i. e. Nagadeva). Sārvādhikāri Chaṇḍi Śeṭṭi, son of Annamelli Seṭṭi granted toll incomes in Kūṇḍi-nāḍu and other countries under his administration. The details of the date are:- Saka 1168, Visvasu, Jyeshtha su. 12, Monday. The details are regular for Saka 1168 (expired) Parābhava in which year they corresponded to Monday, May 28, A. ಕೌಂಡಿನ್ಯ ತಪೋಧನ ಭೂಷಣಂ ಧನ್ಯಂಸಹಜೋಚಿತ ಸೌಖ್ಯಂ ಮಂತ್ರಿಶ್ವರಂ11 ನದೋದ್ಯನ್ಮುಖಂ ಶ್ರೀ ಪದ್ಮನಾಭಂ ಗುಣವತ್ತಮಂ ತತ್ಸತತನ್ಯತಶರ್ಮಯುಗಾಂಭೀರಜಾತ ಸಂಲಗ್ನ ಮಾನಸಭೃಂಗಂ12 ತೃರಂ ಚಾರು ನಾಭಿನಸಂಭಾರದಿಂ ದಿವಾರಾತ್ರಿ ಜನ್ಮಸಂ ಪೂಜಿತಾಯುಧಂ ||ಅತನ ಸೂನು ದಾನಗುಣ ನಿಜ್ಞಾತ ನಿಜ್ಜರಂ13 ತ ಕುಲಾಭ್ಯುದಯಂ ರತ್ನಕಾನದವಾಧ್ಯಕ್ಷನು ಪಾಶಪಂಶಾತ ನಿನ್ನಗ ಭೀರು ಮಕರಧ್ವಜಭಿಪ್ರಜಾರಸನ್ನಿಭ ನಜ್ಜಟ14 ಗುಣನೋರು ಜಮೂಪತಿ ನಾನಗೆನೊವುತಂ || ಕಂ|| ಜನಿಸಿ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿ ಮಾಲಗಾಣೆಜನಕಂ ಶ್ರೀ ದೀವಾಳರಂ ತನಗೆ ಕುಲಾಲಗನೆ ಜ15 ರಸ ಲೊಯಿನೆ ನಾಗಾವಾಸನವನೊಲ್ಲೊಲು ಕೃತಕೃತ್ಯಂ || ಗುರು ನಿತ್ಯಾನಂದಪ್ರಭುಪರದ್ಯೆನ ತನಗೆ ವಿಷ್ಟುನೆನೆ ಧನ್ಯಂ ಶ್ರೀ ವರದ ಜ[ನಾ]16 ಬರುಹ [ಪರಂ] ಗ ದ್ವಿರೇಫನಾಗಜಮೂಷಂ || ಪ್ರ || ಶರಣಂ ಸಾಶ್ವತ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಕಶರಣಂ ವೇದೋಕ್ತಮಾರ್ಗಾತ್ಮಾಕಾರಣಂ ಸ್ಯಾಜಕರಣ ಸ್ಫುರದಿ17 ಬ್ಜಾಪವೃತ್ತಿ ರತ್ನಾಕರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಂ ರಸಕುಲಕಾಲಸಹಸ್ರಕೇತನಂ ತಾಲೇರಣಂ ತಾನೆ[ಸೋ] ನಾಗದೇವನ ಜಗದ್ಯಂದಂ ಪೆಪ್ಪವೃಂದ್ಯ || ಸ್ಯ18 ಜಗಣ್ಯನಸ್ತು ಮಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯಂ ಸರವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ ಪ್ರಭುಪದ ಲಕ್ಯಲಿತತಾವ್ಯತಂ ಫಲಭರಪ್ರತೋಷಿತಾನೇಕ ಲೋಕಜನಂ ಪಂಡಿತ ಪಾರಿ19 ವಂ ಶ್ರೀ ನಾಗದೇವಂ ಗುಣಬ್ರಜ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಿ ಯಶಃಸುಧಾಂಬುನಿಧಿ ಪುರವಾಲ ಮದ್ಯಸ್ಕಿತಂ || ವ || ಮತ್ಸಮನಂತರದ ವಿಶರಣಂ ನಿರಂತರ ಚಕತನನು20 ರೊಮಣೋರಾಜನುಂ ಪಂಡಿತರಾಜನಾತನು ಭಾರಿಶಸಮಲ್ಲಾ ಸನ್ನಿಜ್ಞತ ಕೃತಕೃನುಂ ರಾಯಕುಲತಿಲಕನಾಗನುಂ ಶ್ರೀ ಮನ್ನಾರಾಯಣ್ ಸಮಾ . .21 ಪರಿಪೃತಪಾದಪಂಕೇರುಹಂ ಪ್ರಜಂತುಮಂಡಳೇಜರಾಜನುಂ ಆದರಕ ದ್ವಿಜಾತಿವ್ಯಾದ ಪರಂಪರಾ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ ಸಂಪುಣ್ಯ ಸಂಪ್ರತ್ಯುಪೋಷಿತ[ಜ್ಜ]22 ಮಂಡಳನುಂ ರಿಯಧರಪಾಲನಾಲಮನಿನ್ನಿ ತಂದ ಕೀರ್ತಿಯಂ ದಿಂಗಂತಮಂ ಬಾಸದೆಸುಕೃಂ ತತ್ಕೃತ್ಯನಾಗಿಯುವೊದೆಲು ಶ್ರೀ ನಾಗದೇವ23 ಚಮೂಪತಿಂ [ಜ] ಗದ್ದಿನಸನ್ನಿಧಸನಿಪ ಜನಾಧನಂ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆಯಂ ಮಾಡಿದನದೆಂತನೆ || ಗದ್ಯ || ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಶ್ರೀ ಶಕ ವರುಷ ೧೧೫೪ ನೆಯ ವಿಶ್ವಾ ವಸುಸಂವತ್ಸರದ [ಕೈ]24 ಷ್ಟ ದ್ವಾದಶಿ ಸೋಮವಾರದೊಳ್ || ನಿ || ಮಿಸುಗುವ ಕಾತಕವಿಯ್ಯಪುರದಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಾಧನ ದೇವನವಂ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿಸಿ ನಿಖಿಲ ದ್ವಿಜನ್ಮಹೃದಯಾಂಬು25 ಜ ದೊಳದು ಪದ್ಯದೊಂ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿಸಿ ಹರಹಸಗಾಂ ನಿಕೇತೃತಿಯಾಗಿ ಶ್ರೀ ಜಗಂಗೆಳಲುಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿದನ ಪ್ರದಕ್ಷಿಣೆನೆ ನಾ-26 ಗಜಮೂತಕ ಲೋಕೇಶವೃತ್ತಂ || ವಚನ || ಅಂಕಿಸ ಶ್ರೀ ವರದ ಜನನಾರ್ಥದೇವಜಕ್ಕವತ್ರಿ ಭೂಮ್ಯಾನಭಿಲಂಗೆ ರಂಗಭೋಗಗಳ ಕತ್ತಿನಿಯ27 ಪುರದ ಮಾನ್ಯಮ್ಯಾಜಾಜನಗಳು ತಮ ಪ್ರಥಮಸ್ಥಳದಲು ಕಡವಿನಕಳಿಯಂಪಡುವಲು ಸತ್ಯತಿಯ ದಶಕ ದ್ವಿತೀಯದಿಂ ಬಡಗಲು ಬಾ-28 ಲಕ್ಷಣ ದೇವ ಕೆಯ್ಯಂ ಮೂಡಲು ಪಟ್ಟಿದೊರೆಯಿಂ ತೇಕಲು ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಕೆಯ್ಯ ಕದಿಮಣಕವ್ಯಂ ೧೦೦೦ ಊರುಂ ಪಡುವಲು ಹೆಲ್ಲದಿಂ ಬಡಗಲು29 ಕೊಟ್ಟ ವೃತ್ತವನ ಹೋದೊಂಟ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದಿಂ ಬಡಗಲು ಆಜಯ್ಯಗಳ ಹೊನೆರಡುನೀಳದ ಮನೆ ಗ ಮತ್ಸಮಾ ದೇವಗೇ ದೆಹಾರಿ ಮಾ-30 ಧವ ಭಟ್ಟರ್ ಕ್ರಾತ್ತಿಚಾರಾಧನೆಗೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಮೂಲಸ್ಥಾನದೊರಿಯಂ ನಿಜವತಿತಿ ಪಡತಿ ಕಣಗಣಿ ವಗದ ಮನೆ ಗ ಮತ್ಸಮಾ ಮಹಾಜನಗಳಗಾಣಕ್ಕೆ [ಹ] ಣ ೨೦ || || ಗೋಜ ಮಾತುಲ ಕೆಡಿ-31 ನಾಡು ಕಂಬಾಜರಲು ಆವ . . ಲದೇವನ . . ನದಲು ಗಾನ ೧೦ ಕೊಟ್ಟ[ರ್]ದೇವ ಕೃಯ್ಯಮೂಪ[ದಿ]ಕೇತುಳ ಆಯದಾಯವನ [ಆ] ಗಿಡದ ಮತ್ಸಮಾಸ್ಥಳದ ತೆಳಗ ಸೋಯಿ ನೆಟ್ಟ ತಾಮರಕಯ್ಯ32 ಲು ಆಲು ಹೋಗಿ ಬ್ಜಾವಾದವಾಗಿ [ಮಾದಿ]ದ] ಗುಗುವಿನ ದೇವಕ ತಳೋದಾರಿಯಿಂದವಟಿಕಂ ಗರ ೧೦೦ ಮಂ ಕೊಟ್ಟಿಕೆ ಕೆಟ್ಟಿನ ಮತ್ಸಮಾಮದುಶನ ಮಹಾಜನಗಳ ಕಾಲಗ್ರಾಮದೇವ ತೋಟಕ್ಕೆ ವಳದ ಮೂಲ33 ಹೊನಂ ಬ್ಜಾವಾದದೊಳೆ ಗಂ ೧೦೦ ಮಂ ಕೊಟ್ಟನ್ | ಮತ್ತ . . . ನಾಗರಸರ ತಮಗೇ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಮೀದೇವಸರ ಧಾರಾಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಸನವದತ್ತಿಯನಿನ ದಾರಿಯೊಂ ಪಡುವಲ್ ಕಟ್ಯಸರ ಹಲ್ಲದಿಂ ಬದಗೆ [ಕ] ಲ್ಲ ನಡಿಸಿಕೊಟ್ಟ ಕೆಯ್ಯ ಕಂ ೭೦೦ ಅ34 ಬಳಯ ಮನೆ ೧ || ಮತ್ತಂ ಅಂಬಲಿ ಸೈಟ್ಟಿಯರವರ ಹಸಡಿಯಲು ಹಿರಿಯಹಸಡಿಯ ಮೋದಣಸೀಮೆಯಂ ಮಂಡಳ ಅಸಗಣ್ಯಂ ಬದಗಳ ಬೀದ-ಗೌಡನ ಮನ್ನದಿಂ ತೆಂಕಲ್ ಕಲ್ಲ ನಡಿಸಿ ಕೊ-35 ಟ್ಟೆ ಕೆಯಿ ಕಂ ౧౦౦ ಆ ಬಳಿಯ ಮನೆ ೧ || ಮತ್ತು ಹಿರಿಯ(ವು)ಹೆಸುಡಿಯ ಮಹಾಜನಮಂ ಹಂಬಿಟ್ಟಾರಂ ಕುದೆರೆಯು[ಬಾ]ಗಂ ಹಳ್ಳದ ಮಂಡಲ ಎದೆಮಯ ದಾರಿಯಂ ತೆಂಕಲು ಕಲ್ಲ ನಡಿಸಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟೆ ಕೆಯಿ ಕಂ ౧౦౦ ಆ ಬಳಿಯ ಮನೆ ೧ ||36 ದೇವಗೆ ಆ ಅಂಜಮಣ್ಗೆಟ್ಟಿಯರ ಮಗ ಶ್ರೀಮತ್ಸಬ್ಬಾಧಿಕಾರಿ ಚೌಡಸೆಟ್ಟಿಯರುತಮ್ಮಣ್ಣಯ್ಯನ ದೇಶಗಳಿಳು ಕೊಂಡಿನಾಡು ಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಎಲ್ಲಿ ಎನ ಹೆಜದಡ್ಯಸಂಕ ಪರಿಹರವೆಂದು ನಾಡಸಾ-37 ಮ್ಯವಂತರ ನೆರೆದು ಪ[ಟ್ಟಾ] ಯವಾಗಿ ಬಿಟ್ಟ ಕಣ್ಗಾಣ ౧౦ ಮಂಗಳ ಮಹಾಶ್ರೀ ಶ್ರೀ || ಮತ್ಸಮಸ್ತಳದ ಮಹಾಜನಗಳಿಗುಂ ಆ ನಾಗರಾಜನು ಶ್ರೀ ಜನಾರ್ದ್ದನದೇವಗೆ ದರ್ಶನವಾಗಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟೆ ಕೆಯಿ-38 ನೊಂದು ಹೊಂಸೊಣಗೆ ಕಾಳಿಕೆ ಗ ೧ ಕ್ರಯದವಸಕ್ಕೆ ಗ ೧೦ ನಂ . . . . ಊರಮ . . . . . . . . . . . ದಶಕದ ವೃತ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಬಾಯಿಯ ಗ ಬಡ-ಗಣ ಸಪ್ಪಿತಿಯ.39 ವಹ ಮನೆ ಅಕ್ಕಿಣಿ ಆಣಾಮ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಬಳಸುವ ಹಡಿಕೆ ಮಣಜಣೆಯಾಗಿ ಸೌ[ಜ] .ಕ್ಕೆ ಸರ್ವಬಾಧಾಪರಿಹಾರವಾಗಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟರು ||

cells.remarks: Hero-stone standing near Jain Basti. ? A. D. 1381. This hero-stone introduces the imperial king [Hari]raya Devaraya- odeya as ruling over a kingdom bounded by four oceans, and having such titles as: Raya-rajaguru and Raya-vadipitamaha. Hadapada Naganna- odeya is mentioned as his feudatory ruling over Haiva and Konkana from his capital at Honnaura. The record states that Naganna-odeya led an expedition in Durmukhi, Saka 1300, against Mahamanda- lesvara Kesavadeva-odeya of Nagira who bore the epithets "hand to the faces of the heroes", "scarer of army-camps" and "lord of the throne of the Siddhas". In the encounter that followed one Jakanna-nayaka, son of Bommanna-nayaka's son [Vodi]sara-nayaka, is stated to have died giving a heroic front to the enemy, whereupon Bommanna-naya- ka's son set up a stone to his memory. If Durmukhi is a mistake for Durmati which corresponded to Saka 1303, the date of the record would fall in A. D. 1381. No further details of date are given in the inscription. The Saka and cyclic years are evidently a wrong citation. I Section. II Section III Section IV Section V Section (1) The writing is badly obliterated from line 8 onwards.
